title: Identifiability of a dissipative knowledge-dynamics model: exact recovery under designed excitation, degeneration on observational data
abstract: Human learning is a dissipative dynamical process: mastery accumulates through practice, decays through forgetting, and propagates across interdependent concepts. We model it as a nonlinear dissipative system of ordinary differential equations whose parameters are mechanistically meaningful (a transfer-of-practice matrix, per-concept forgetting rates, and a saturating practice-response gain), and we study when those parameters can actually be recovered from data. For two concepts, we prove a constructive structural identifiability theorem for the associated inverse problem under explicit excitation conditions, together with monotonicity, robustness and L-stability results. We derive an implicit L-stable scheme and a batched solver numerically equivalent to the per-trajectory formulation yet two orders of magnitude faster. The empirical study is two-sided. Under the theorem's excitation conditions, synthetic recovery is exact. On large observational benchmarks it is not. An apparently strong recovery, with forgetting rates correlating with topic error rates at Spearman $ρ= 0.83$, is refuted by four controls: it survives destroying the temporal order of the data, is matched by a classical Bayesian baseline, and is unaffected by removing real timestamps. A single shared forgetting rate attains the same accuracy, and replaying the real schedule with identical true rates reproduces most of the correlation. A positive control shows that the controls detect forgetting where it is observable. We trace the effect to the stationary structure of the model and show that it is consistent with the degeneration anticipated by the theory in the absence of designed excitation.

title: KVerus: Scalable and Resilient Formal Verification Proof Generation for Rust Code
abstract: Repository-scale formal verification is becoming practical for Rust systems, but maintaining and extending proofs remains expensive in real projects. In the Asterinas Rust OS kernel, the CortenMM memory-management module requires Verus proofs that cross file and module boundaries, reuse project-specific lemmas with limited documentation, and survive frequent Verus/toolchain evolution. Existing LLM-based proof-generation methods are mostly designed for small or single-file tasks, and they do not provide the structural project knowledge or verifier-aware repair needed in such a repository-scale verification workflow.

title: 自由能原理、注意力-Gibbs 桥与截断采样（Top-k/Min-P）：一个构造性机器检查视角
abstract: ## 摘要（Abstract） 本工作报告了 ConstructiveWorld 库中自由能原理（FEP）数学核、softmax 注意力与 Gibbs 分布之间的精确桥接，以及 KV 缓存逐出、top-k 截断与 Min-P 截断的构造性定量定理。全部证明在纯构造性逻辑下完成（零 Axiom、零 Admitted，仅依赖 Coq 标准库），共享同一 Cauchy 实数 / Boltzmann 分布 / KL 散度基座。核心贡献为三条主线：**(i) 温度参数化的最大熵对偶闭合（定理 4.6a–4.6e）**——对每个温度参数 t，约束熵最大化解的存在唯一性与温度-能量严格单调均被证明，核心为对称 KL 恒等 `(β1−β2)(E2−E1) == KL(p2‖p1) + KL(p1‖p2)`；**(ii) Top-k 截断的总变差（total variation, TV）精确恒等（定理 7.6，TV == tail_mass/Z_thermo）与 Min-P 截断的定量刻画（定理 8.9：dropped ≤ 1 − 1/|S|，且为熵界 dropped ≤ 1 − e^{−S} 的推论）**——截断误差的定量刻画而非仅定性记账；**(iii) 构造性 LPO 规避机制**——以弱三分 `real_weak_trich` 替代排中律、以逐 eps 余量替代“非严格且不趋近”陈述、误差累积恰为 eps（而非 |S|·eps）的归一化论证。此外，把 softmax 注意力层的迭代视为 Markov 链时的 TV 收缩与迭代收敛已在 Doeblin minorization 假设（δ ∈ (0,1)，核 ≥ δ·稳态质量）下机器检查，显式几何率 (1−δ)ⁿ：`attention_tv_contraction`、`attention_tv_iter_contraction`与 `attention_iterate_converges`全部 Qed；该簇的更一般双点形态（`u_tv_contraction` / `u_tv_iter`：免平稳性、免详细平衡、免 `transition_nonneg`、免 μ 非负，参考分布只需任意归一化）与有界 logits softmax 注意力核上的显式 Doeblin 实例化（`bs_minorization`，δ* := e^{−2Δ/T}；显式收缩率 (1 − e^{−2Δ/T})ⁿ：`bounded_softmax_tv_contraction` / `bounded_softmax_tv_iter`）亦已机器检查（见 §5.5 定理 5.4–5.6）。库内进一步在模块化扩展层闭合：温度窗口 T→∞ 半边（`temp_window_T_infty`：∀eps>0 存在 T₂>0，∀T>T₂ 时温度化权重对均匀分布的 TV ≤ eps——与 T→0 硬注意力极限构成「硬注意力–均匀混合」温度两极合龙，§5.4(a)）、KV 逐出核的有限 n 漂移界（`kv_drift_bound`：TV(K_evⁿμ, Kⁿμ) ≤ n·c + eps，∀n 有限步、无平稳性主张，§6.2.2）以及 Q/K 范数界到 双界 logits的显式转化（`qk_logits_bounded`，根有界前提形态，§5.5 定理 5.8）。支撑层包括：变分自由能分解、Gibbs 不等式与等号条件、Boltzmann 分布的自由能最小化唯一性、ELBO 下界与紧性条件、softmax 注意力即 Gibbs 分布的精确对应（单位温度、任意温度，以及缩放-温度对偶 `scale_temp_duality`：任意 c>0 下以 1/c 缩放 logits 的 softmax == 温度 c 的 softmax，把 Transformer 的 `1/√d` 缩放的 logits 层形态闭合；`√d` 覆盖已两层全闭：抽象层任意平方维数 d=k² 的见证实例化已机器检查（`sqrt_witness_nat_sq`、`scale_dual_nat_sq_k`），Real 层任意 d ≥ 0（含非平方）的构造性平方根 `real_sqrt_exists` 已证明，抽象 Id 层任意非负 d 的见证实例化亦已闭合（`sqrt_witness_exists_abstract`，模块 `UpDebtSqrtAbs`）；见 §5.4）、KV 逐出导致的稳态偏差的恒等式控制（Set 层主体为三角不等式记账，见 §6.2；另有破缺恒为零的正结果与有限 n 漂移界，见 §6.2.2；温度-Lipschitz 定量界由 Real 层定理 6.1b/6.1c 承载，见 §6.2.1）、top-k 截断的主化（majorization）最优性，以及 Min-P 截断采样的可判定性、非空性、核归一化（`minp_markov_kernel_normalized`）与相对完整 softmax 核的单调性（见 §8）。`free_energy_kl_decomp` 与 `rlhf_free_energy_kl`为同一自由能-KL 分解的两次实例化，故本工作与 RLHF/DPO 对齐目标共享同一数学基座。本文给出核心定理陈述、证明策略概述、与相关形式化工作的对比，并明确声明当前边界。**关于实例化（诚实边界）**：本文定理在实数接口 `RealInterfaceEnhanced`（Id 相等）上陈述；该接口的 setoid 对应物已由具体柯西实数端到端实例化（`Real_RealInterfaceSetoid`；`RealEnhancedReal`，字段全部实值化），部分头条定理另有 Real 层逐 eps 直接复刻（`real_gibbs_inequality_eps`、`real_attention_is_gibbs` 等）；抽象定理签名向 setoid 实例的整体迁移（已有定理级试点两件，§10.2 第 1 项）、以及抽象陈述与 Real 层复刻之间的 statement-level 机器对齐仍为开放工作（逐字段/逐定理对照见附录 C，详情见 §9.2 与 §10.2）。 --- **Abstract (English)** This work reports the machine-checked formalization of the mathematical core of the Free Energy Principle (FEP), the exact bridge between softmax attention and Gibbs distributions, and constructive quantitative theorems for KV-cache eviction, top-k truncation, and Min-P truncation inside the ConstructiveWorld library. All proofs are carried out in pure constructive logic (zero Axioms, zero Admitted proof obligations, relying only on the Coq standard library) and share a common base of Cauchy reals, Boltzmann distributions, and KL divergence. The core contributions form three threads: (i) the closure of the temperature-parameterized maximum-entropy duality (Theorems 4.6a–4.6e), proving existence and uniqueness of the constrained entropy maximizer for each temperature parameter together with strict temperature–energy monotonicity, centered on the symmetric KL identity (β1−β2)(E2−E1) = KL(p2‖p1) + KL(p1‖p2); (ii) the exact total-variation (TV) identity for top-k truncation (Theorem 7.6, TV = tail_mass/Z_thermo) and the quantitative characterization of Min-P truncation (Theorem 8.9: dropped ≤ 1 − 1/|S|, a corollary of the entropy bound dropped ≤ 1 − e^{−S}), giving quantitative characterizations of truncation error rather than qualitative bookkeeping; (iii) a constructive mechanism for avoiding LPO, replacing the law of excluded middle by the weak trichotomy `real_weak_trich`, replacing “non-strict and non-converging” statements by per-eps slack, and showing that error accumulation is exactly eps (rather than |S|·eps) through a normalization argument. In addition, viewing the iteration of the softmax attention layer as a Markov chain, total-variation contraction and iterative convergence are machine-checked under a Doeblin minorization assumption (δ ∈ (0,1), kernel ≥ δ · stationary mass), with explicit geometric rate (1−δ)ⁿ: `attention_tv_contraction`, `attention_tv_iter_contraction`, and `attention_iterate_converges`, all closed with Qed. A recent library extension further machine-checks a genuinely more general two-point form of this family (`u_tv_contraction` / `u_tv_iter`: no stationarity, no detailed balance, no `transition_nonneg`, no non-negativity of μ, reference distribution only required to be normalized) together with an explicit Doeblin instantiation on bounded-logit softmax attention kernels (`bs_minorization` with δ* := e^{−2Δ/T}; explicit contraction rate (1 − e^{−2Δ/T})ⁿ via `bounded_softmax_tv_contraction` / `bounded_softmax_tv_iter`), all closed with Qed (see §5.5, Theorems 5.4–5.6). Supporting layers include the variational free-energy decomposition, the Gibbs inequality and equality condition, uniqueness of the Boltzmann distribution as the free-energy minimizer, the ELBO lower bound and tightness condition, the exact correspondence between softmax attention and the Gibbs distribution (at unit temperature, at arbitrary temperature, and via the scale–temperature duality `scale_temp_duality`: for every c > 0, softmax with logits scaled by 1/c equals softmax at temperature c, closing the logits-level shape of the Transformer 1/√d scaling, with √d coverage now closed at both layers: machine-checked witness instances for every square dimension d = k² at the abstract layer (`sqrt_witness_nat_sq` and `scale_dual_nat_sq_k`), a constructive square root for every d ≥ 0 at the Real layer, including non-square d (`real_sqrt_exists`), and an abstract-layer witness instantiation for every non-negative d (`sqrt_witness_exists_abstract`, module `UpDebtSqrtAbs`)); see §5.4.An identity-based control of the steady-state deviation caused by KV-cache eviction (whose Set-layer content is the triangle inequality; see §6.2, while the temperature–Lipschitz quantitative bounds are carried by Real-layer Theorems 6.1b/6.1c in §6.2.1), the majorization optimality of top-k truncation, and the decidability, non-emptiness, normalization (`minp_markov_kernel_normalized`), and monotonicity relative to the full softmax kernel of Min-P truncated sampling (see §8).Since `free_energy_kl_decomp` and `rlhf_free_energy_kl` instantiate the same free-energy–KL decomposition, this work shares one mathematical base with RLHF/DPO alignment objectives. We present the core theorem statements, outline proof strategies, compare with related formalization work, and explicitly declare current boundaries. **On instantiation (honest boundary)**: the headline theorems are stated over the real-number interface `RealInterfaceEnhanced` (with `Id` equality); the setoid counterparts of this interface are end-to-end instantiated on concrete Cauchy reals (`Real_RealInterfaceSetoid`,; `RealEnhancedReal`,, all fields filled with real-valued constructions), and several headline theorems additionally have direct Real-layer per-eps replicas (`real_gibbs_inequality_eps`, `real_attention_is_gibbs`, etc.). The wholesale migration of abstract theorem statements onto the setoid instances, and a machine-checked statement-level alignment between abstract statements and Real-layer replicas, remain open work (see Appendix C for the per-field/per-theorem comparison table; details in §9.2 and §10.2). ---

title: How Much Human Review Does AI Data Entry Need? Guaranteed-Error Automation with Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Organizations that use machine learning to automate data entry face a practical question: which predictions can be accepted automatically and which must be checked by a person? A common answer is a fixed confidence cut-off, such as accepting every prediction made with at least 90% confidence. This paper evaluates that practice against threshold-selection procedures with a statistical guarantee on the error rate of automatically accepted records. Using four public datasets (BANKING77, CLINC150, AG News and Adult), eight dataset–model combinations and 500 random calibration/test splits each, we find that a fixed 0.90 cut-off is unreliable: it automated between 18.5% and 82.5% of records depending on the model and, for two combinations, exceeded a 2% error target in every run. Choosing the threshold from a sample of checked records without a safety margin exceeded the error target in 34–57% of runs, and collecting more checked records did not fix this. In contrast, a Learn-then-Test procedure with exact binomial p-values, which we combine with a hybrid multiple-testing scheme, exceeded a 5% error target in at most 3.6% of runs (the allowed rate was 5%) while automating 58–85% of records using 1,000 checked examples. About 500 checked records were needed before useful automation became possible (63% of records automated on average), and 1% error targets could not be certified with 1,000 records. When 20% of live inputs were of an unexpected type, a threshold calibrated on clean data exceeded the 5% target in 95–96% of runs, whereas calibrating on a sample of realistic traffic restored the guarantee. We conclude with practical guidance for deploying human-in-the-loop automation with a verifiable error budget.

title: ConsensusCourt: Procedural Evidence Arbitration for Scientific Claims in Multi-Agent Research Pipelines (v0.4.17)
abstract: Open-source companion to the preprint ConsensusCourt: Procedural Evidence Arbitration for Scientific Claims in Multi-Agent Research Pipelines (v0.4.17, September 21, 2026). Contains the manuscript sources and compiled PDF (paper/), the court/baseline/rubric implementations under test (code/core/), one deterministic experiment pipeline per paper table and figure (code/scripts/), the pytest suites and DDB benchmark generators (code/tests/), and every machine-readable report backing the manuscript's numbers (code/data/). ConsensusCourt borrows its procedural guarantees from the courtroom rather than voting theory: an asymmetric burden of proof (claims are presumed innocent until a detected contradiction pair convicts them), a source-pedigree evidence scorer whose confidence channel is structurally decoupled from conviction, a three-state (pass/fail/unknown) citation-verification policy that holds the clean-claim false-positive rate at 0 under verification failure rates up to 100%, and an escalation layer routing unadjudicable cases to human review. The benchmark and red-line experiments are deterministic (seed = 42) and zero-LLM; entry point: run_v03_regression.sh. Code, tests, and data are MIT-licensed; the manuscript under paper/ is All Rights Reserved (arXiv perpetual non-exclusive license selected at submission).

title: A Taxonomy of Label-Efficient Learning with Foundation Models
abstract: This survey examines how unlabeled data is used across semi-supervised learning, weak supervision, in-context learning, and foundation-model adaptation. It organizes 95 works in a 16-cell taxonomy based on where unlabeled data enters the learning process and the source of inductive bias. The survey distinguishes exact reductions from structural analogies, identifies sparsely studied combinations, and provides a regime-based decision table grounded in the original experimental evidence.

title: KETERBACAAN BUKU TEKS GAYENG BASA JAWA KELAS X MENGGUNAKAN TEKNIK CLOZE TEST DI SMA AL-I’TISHOM BOARDING SCHOOL
abstract: The Gayeng Basa Jawa textbook serves as a primary instructional material for Javanese language learning at the senior high school level. However, its readability level and appropriateness for students in boarding school environments with diverse linguistic backgrounds have not been thoroughly examined. This study aims to analyze the readability level of texts in the Gayeng Basa Jawa textbook for tenth-grade students and describe its alignment with students' reading abilities at SMA Al-I'tishom Boarding School Grabag. The research employed a descriptive quantitative design utilizing the cloze test technique through a synonymy scoring approach. A total sampling technique was applied to recruit 17 tenth-grade students as respondents, with six Latin-script texts selected across six chapters serving as textual data. The cloze instruments omitted every third word mechanically regardless of grammatical function. The findings revealed that three texts fell into the instructional category, while the other three reached the independent level. The overall mean readability score was 58.9%, positioning the textbook within the instructional threshold. Consequently, the textbook is appropriate for classroom use, though active teacher mediation remains necessary to help students decipher unfamiliar archaic and borrowed vocabulary. ABSTRAK Buku teks Gayeng Basa Jawa merupakan salah satu bahan ajar utama dalam pembelajaran Bahasa Jawa di tingkat Sekolah Menengah Atas (SMA). Namun, kesesuaian tingkat keterbacaannya dengan kemampuan siswa di sekolah asrama dengan latar belakang bahasa ibu yang beragam belum banyak dikaji secara empiris. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis tingkat keterbacaan wacana dalam buku teks Gayeng Basa Jawa kelas X serta mendeskripsikan kesesuaiannya dengan kemampuan membaca siswa di SMA Al-I'tishom Boarding School Grabag. Metode yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif deskriptif dengan teknik cloze test menggunakan pendekatan synonymy methods. Pengambilan sampel dilakukan menggunakan teknik total sampling terhadap 17 siswa kelas X sebagai responden, dengan data berupa enam wacana beraksara Latin dari enam bab buku teks tersebut. Instrumen penelitian berupa tes rumpang yang melesapkan kata ketiga secara konsisten tanpa memperhatikan fungsi kata. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tiga wacana berada pada tingkat instruksional dan tiga wacana berada pada tingkat independen. Rata-rata skor keterbacaan keseluruhan wacana adalah 58,9%, yang menempatkan buku teks ini pada kategori instruksional. Dengan demikian, buku teks ini layak digunakan sebagai bahan ajar, tetapi siswa tetap memerlukan pendampingan guru untuk memahami kosakata arkais dan istilah serapan yang belum familier.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Google Play Reviews of Online Lending Platforms in Indonesia
abstract: Sentiment analysis is often useful for grouping sentiments and understanding the general perspective toward a particular topic. There are several models developed for online lending platforms. However, they do not focus on Indonesia, which might have unique characteristics compared to other countries. This paper presents a sentiment analysis model focusing on Indonesian online lending platforms. It features either multinomial naïve bayes, logistic regression, and support vector machine (SVM). Based on our evaluation of 10,000 reviews, our sentiment analysis model achieves approximately 85% precision and 90% recall. The model is highly effective. Our analysis of the reviews shows that while many borrowers appreciate the time efficiency and accessibility, some perceive the platforms as predatory, using aggressive and unethical debt-collection tactics.

title: From Models to Workflows: Communicating Agentic AI in Asset Management
abstract: Agentic AI creates a new communication problem for asset managers: stakeholders need to understand not only what a model produced, but how the workflow around it was built, checked, and signed off. As access to foundation models becomes less differentiated across large institutions, sophisticated stakeholders increasingly ask not only whether a model is accurate, but what evidence the analysis rests on, what checks were run, and where accountability sits. A fluent AI-supported output can hide that entire chain. This article proposes three workflow controls—grounding, stability, and permissioning—and a compact disclosure record that travels with each AI-supported investment output, keeping what the model produced separate from what the firm approved. Operationally, these controls help keep unsupported, unstable, or unauthorized AI-supported outputs from entering the investment process. Communicatively, they give a firm a concrete language for explaining its AI-supported investment processes: what the workflow read, whether its conclusions are repeatable, what it could and could not do, and where human judgment entered. This is a framework for explaining and supervising AI-supported investment workflows, not a performance claim or a certification: it makes the process auditable, and accountability for investment decisions stays with the people who make them.

title: Rare earth minerals occurrence in Zarigan Granite, Chadormalu mining area, Bafq Region, Central Iran, using multispectral and hyperspectral data
abstract: Monazite and xenotime are the main rare earth element (REE)–bearing minerals, typically extracted from placer deposits but also occurring in granitic rocks that act as their source. This study aims to map and conduct an initial evaluation of monazite minerals and REEs within the weathered and eroded sediments of the Zarigan Granite, located in the northern part of the Chadormalu paleocrater, Central Iran. Multispectral and hyperspectral datasets from ASTER, Sentinel-2 MSI, and PRISMA were employed to assess their capability in identifying and mapping REE-bearing minerals. Image processing techniques including the Minimum Noise Fraction (MNF) transform, Mathematical Evaluation Method (MEM), Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM), and band ratio analysis were applied to the VNIR and SWIR spectral ranges. The comparative results indicate that the band ratio technique applied to PRISMA data provided the most reliable discrimination of monazite and REE occurrences in the Chadormalu paleocrater and the adjacent alluvial plain. These findings demonstrate that PRISMA’s hyperspectral capabilities offer an effective framework for REE mineral mapping in arid granitic terrains.

title: Diagnosing and Recovering from Observation-Space Shift at Long-Horizon Skill Seams
abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation is often built by chaining independently trained skills. Although each skill can be reliable in isolation, performance degrades sharply when skills are chained: each downstream skill must start from the state its predecessor leaves behind rather than from its training distribution. We study this failure mode, Observation-Space Shift (OSS), and ask what causes these skill-seam failures. Using privileged simulator resets, we find that the dominant shift comes from displaced scene state (e.g., an open drawer or secondary objects left behind by earlier skills), not from the robot's joint configuration or the object the downstream skill manipulates. To test this diagnosis, we build a fully learned detect-restore-resume system: a task-progress monitor detects the stall, a learned policy restores the displaced scene components, and seam-robust fine-tuning lets the skill resume. It recovers the seam where every tested alternative fails, which we treat as evidence for the diagnosis rather than as a general-purpose method. On the BOSS-44 benchmark, the system improves full-chain success from 7.6% to 26.5%, a 3.5x improvement over the base policy and 51% of a privileged restoration oracle, whereas best-of-K resampling, a Diffusion Policy, and world-model baselines fail to recover from the evaluated seam states. On a real Franka arm running a fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ policy, the same monitor is limited by exterior-camera observability, yet closing the loop still recovers some otherwise-terminal failures, motivating wrist and gripper sensing. These results suggest that some long-horizon composition failures are better addressed by restoring the scene before resuming the policy than by retrying from an off-support state.

title: TaoD2C-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Industrial UI Code Generation Beyond Visual Fidelity
abstract: A key challenge for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is moving beyond visual recognition to constraint-aware cross-modal reasoning. This involves combining visual cues with information from other modalities to understand elements' relationships under domain-specific rules. This challenge is acutely evident in industrial design-to-code (D2C), which converts user interface (UI) designs into code and requires MLLMs to connect design images with disorganized layer metadata, infer component and layout implementation requirements, and realize them in code under target-library constraints. However, these capabilities remain insufficiently evaluated in realistic industrial settings. To fill this gap, we present TaoD2C-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs' ability to generate UI code that satisfies implementation requirements in industrial applications. The TaoD2C dataset consists of 2,861 production designs from 17 commercial platforms with 97,652 expert annotations across four categories: Component, Group, Alignment, and Position. These annotations distinguish required constraints from permitted implementation choices. TaoD2C-Bench defines three tasks: end-to-end UI code generation, requirement inference, and requirement realization. Evaluating eight MLLMs reveals substantial gaps in generating UI code that satisfies implementation requirements, alongside distinct performance profiles in inference and realization. We further show that MLLMs' visual reconstruction ability does not necessarily imply an ability to generate code that meets these requirements. We release TaoD2C to support research on industrial UI code generation.

title: Policy Learning with Weak Signals
abstract: Policy learning in digital experimentation faces three challenges: weak signal-to-noise ratios, rich covariate spaces, and massive data volumes. We formalize this regime by modeling treatment-effect estimates from increasingly fine covariate partitions as Gaussian observations with bounded signal-to-noise ratios. We establish that, in general, the optimal treatment policy is not learnable in this setting. Even learning the optimal policy value suffers from impractically slow rates. However, when treatment effects vary smoothly, we derive minimax-adaptive policies based on linear smoothers that achieve vanishing welfare regret. We demonstrate the practical value of our framework by applying it to large-scale real-world experiments at Netflix, showing that personalized linear-smoothing policies can dominate unpersonalized policies even in this challenging empirical setting.

title: Real-world application of deep learning in large-scale seismic interference attenuation: A case study in the Camie field of Angola
abstract: In marine seismic acquisition, seismic interference (SI) occurs when energy from nearby external seismic source(s) is captured. It typically appears as coherent noise with linear or non-linear movement and varying amplitudes across different sail lines. SI is commonly observed and poses a challenge for seismic data processing. We present a case history of a previously proposed deep neural network (DNN)-based workflow applied for SI attenuation across a marine seismic block in the Camie Field of Angola. This field survey covers over 345 km2 and is marked by the challenge of multiple SI types. The employed DNN-based workflow performs SI attenuation in the common shot domain based on a supervised learning framework: a small subset of the SI-contaminated data was first processed by a conventional geophysical algorithm to obtain an estimate of the SI noise, which was then manually blended with the SI-free common shot gathers from the same survey to generate the training pairs. To ensure signal fidelity, several techniques were applied to improve the DNN's performance. A key highlight of this case history is its scale: this represents a real-world, large-scale processing project and we present a comprehensive comparison of the DNN-based workflow with the conventional geophysical algorithm across the entire survey block, focusing on both processing quality and processing time. The results demonstrate the outstanding performance of the employed DNN-based workflow, which achieved higher SI removal accuracy, with less signal leakage and more complete SI removal. The promising results of this application also open up possibilities for integrating deep learning into other seismic denoising tasks. In addition, we discuss the limitations of this case history, aiming to provide insights for future research and applications in the field.

title: Intelligent Logical Mind (ILM)
abstract: Abstract. This paper reformulates Intelligent Logical Mind (ILM) as an implementable question-to-answer system. The historical ILM design represents a question in a 7×12 character matrix and applies deterministic character transformations before an answer-extraction stage. The present formulation separates that process into two layers. The first is a symbolic transformation layer derived from the historical ILM procedure and selected letter-manipulation concepts documented by the author in an earlier Ilm al-Jafr tutorial. The second is a probabilistic lexical decoder. Its normative input is two final 12-character rows, Muakhar-Sadr and Nazira, arranged as 12 vertical columns. Each column must contribute exactly one output character. A recurrent sequence model assigns context-dependent probabilities to the two source branches of every column. After source selection, AQEG/Iqgh substitutions are permitted only within the selected source character's own domain; diagonal and cross-column substitution are prohibited. title: Adversarial Backpropagation Burning and Zero-Knowledge Non-Ingestion Proofs (zkVM): Deterministic Physical-Layer Interlocks and Prior Art Invalidation Architectures Against Unconsented AI Ingestion
abstract: Abstract (English)Conventional legal and regulatory frameworks governing generative artificial intelligence rely almost exclusively on ex-post judicial remedies: protracted copyright infringement lawsuits, contested fair-use hearings, and discretionary administrative penalties. These mechanisms fail catastrophically against well-capitalized hyperscalers that systematically exploit procedural delays to achieve irreversible weight-space enclosure. This technical monograph establishes a deterministic, physical-layer counter-architecture that replaces linguistic legal disputation with immediate, non-negotiable computational interlocks. First, we formalize the mathematics of "Adversarial Backpropagation Burning" (Backprop-Burn): engineering imperceptible multi-scale perturbations embedded within public text, mathematical specifications, and multimodal assets. When processed by deep neural network encoders during unconsented gradient descent, these perturbations induce catastrophic gradient explosion (||∇_W L|| → ∞) and orthogonal subspace corruption, destroying the host model's latent representation stability and burning millions of dollars of training compute. Second, we design an automated market-gating architecture utilizing Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machines (zkVM). By requiring model providers to furnish non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (π_clean) proving that their committed training dataset root (R_dataset) shares an empty intersection with public cryptographic opt-out registries (H_optout), platforms failing compliance face immediate, network-level circuit breakers and marketplace eviction without human judicial latency. Third, we establish the "Prior Art Minefield" protocol: utilizing CERN Zenodo's immutable timestamps to deploy exhaustively parameterized technical architectures that automatically trigger novelty and non-obviousness rejections during patent office examination, invalidating hostile corporate filings at zero defensive legal cost. This treatise proves that authentic intellectual sovereignty resides in deterministic engineering interlocks that inflict immediate computational self-destruction upon unauthorized exploitation. 和文要旨生成AIおよびフロンティアモデルを巡る従来の法規制枠組みは、事後的な民事訴訟、解釈が分かれるフェアユース審理、および行政裁量による過料勧告という「事後的是正手段」に全面的に依存してきた。しかしこれらの手段は、訴訟遅延と司法のタイムラグを計算に入れ、事実上の既成事実化(重み空間への不可逆的焼き込み)を図る巨大テック企業に対して構造的に無力である。本技術モノグラフは、人間の曖昧な言葉による法廷闘争を排し、侵害行為そのものを計算機・アルゴリズム・物理層レベルで即座に機能不全に追い込む決定論的インターロック・アーキテクチャを確立する。 第一に、「敵対的逆伝播焼却(Backprop-Burn)」の数理モデルを定式化する。公開文書、数理定義、およびマルチモーダルデータ内に、人間の知覚には不可視でありながら、無断で勾配降下法(SGD/AdamW)に投入された瞬間に極端な勾配爆発(||∇_W L|| → ∞)および直交部分空間の重み崩壊を引き起こす敵対的微小摂動(Adversarial Perturbation)を重畳させる。これにより、無断学習を実行したモデル全体の潜在表現を不可逆的に破壊し、数百万〜数千万ドルの計算資源(コンピュート)を物理的に焼却する自律防衛機構を設計する。 第二に、ゼロ知識仮想マシン(zkVM)を活用した自動市場排除ゲートを構築する。モデル提供者に対し、学習データセットのマークルルート(R_dataset)と公認オプトアウト台帳(H_optout)の積集合が空集合であることを立証する非対話型ゼロ知識証明(π_clean)の提出を要求し、証明を提示できないモデルをネットワーク境界層および配信プラットフォームにおいて自動通信遮断する。 第三に、全方位パラメータ先行開示プロトコル「先行技術マインフィールド(Prior Art Minefield)」を策定し、CERN Zenodoの不変タイムスタンプを通じて特許審査官の検索網に先手地雷を敷設することで、後発の企業特許出願を審査段階で100%自動却下・即死させる。本研究は、言葉の議論を超克し、手を出した瞬間に相手を自滅させる物理・暗号論的自己防衛の完成を宣言する。

title: Building a deeply AI over a substrate you cannot retrain: the Clara Nexus reference implementation of layered intelligence theory
abstract: Layered intelligence theory (LIT) specifies eight design principles for what its author terms a Deeply AI—a cognitive architecture whose parameters and surrounding structure jointly instantiate the preconditions for reorganisation, reflection, and falsifiable learning. The specification is silent on how a builder without write access to those parameters might proceed. This paper reports a working reference implementation, the Clara platform, instantiating those principles over hosted frontier large language models. The reference implementation is the platform as a whole rather than any single surface: four surfaces across three substrate vendors—the conversational surfaces (Clara Nexus chat and Clara Companion) on OpenAI substrate models, the reading and instrumentation layer on Anthropic substrate models, a data-sensing path on Perplexity, and an independent read-only Research seat on Claude Sonnet 5—disclosed in full in §2.4, of which Clara Nexus is the primary surface for the constitutional runtime. This is a reference-implementation and specification-conformance paper rather than a benchmark-driven empirical evaluation, and it makes no task-performance claim. Specification conformance, as reported here, means a traceable mapping from a published specification clause to a named runtime carrier—a typed identifier, a function, or a database table—inspectable independently of the author’s description. The eight principles are sorted, as this paper’s analytic contribution, into those describing what the model’s parameters must do, which are structurally unreachable from a hosted substrate, and those describing what the surrounding architecture must do, which are implementable at the scaffold layer. For each principle, there is a record, a verdict of built at scaffold, partial, or substrate-unreachable, alongside the named runtime carrier grounding it or the gap preventing one, and the surface evidencing it. The core engineering contribution is a constitutional runtime: seven fail-closed checks enforced at prompt-composition time, before any call reaches the substrate, encoded as a single assert Constitutional invariant. Six are typed assertions over a structured candidate move, and one is a pattern-matched textual check whose error characteristics are stated rather than assumed. Perceptual control theory primitives are reported as prompt-level Companion voice discipline rather than as a runtime-enforced mechanism. The empirical evaluation of the deployed system belongs to a companion paper whose eight falsifiable predictions are enumerated in §4.3.

title: Semantic Subtext in the Bubble Sort Algorithm
abstract: The bubble sort algorithm is one of the simplest and most well‑known in programming. That is why this algorithm was chosen as an experimental algorithm for studying the meanings embedded in it and their transformation. This research is part of a broader study whose final goal is to develop a system for the automatic generation of algorithms. Automatic algorithm generation can be implemented in various ways, but in this case, preference is given to a semantic approach — more precisely, an approach based on Semantic Web Technologies. The advantage of this approach lies in the direct, “willful” movement (from one concept to another) towards the result, as well as in the ability to trace the entire path from the initial data to the generated algorithm. To achieve the final goal, it is proposed to develop an ontology of the semantic subtext of the algorithm. This ontology will serve as a source of rules for an expert system for the automatic generation of algorithms.

title: Black soldier fly algorithm based on swarm intelligence method for solving optimization problems
abstract: Meta-heuristic swarm algorithms are vital for resolving complex, non-convex optimization problems. However, contemporary optimizers increasingly suffer from structural stagnation and slow convergence rates when tracking highly rugged engineering surfaces; this limitation stems from their strict reliance on standard linear vector updates or basic random walks that cause search agents to blindly bypass narrow global valleys. To overcome this challenge, this paper introduces a novel swarm-based optimization framework named the black soldier fly algorithm (BSFA), modeled after the biological habitat selection, conspecific grouping, and microclimate oviposition tracking behaviors of certain fly species. Unlike traditional systems that apply uniform position updates across the entire population, BSFA introduces a decoupled non-linear position update architecture. Global exploration is governed by a dynamic, non-linear fractional ratio tracking inter-agent spatial density (cohesion) against target proximity (separation). Local exploitation is driven by a unique algebraic cardioid trajectory operator. This mathematical configuration allows individual agents to loop dynamically around target spaces rather than rushing directly toward them, enabling an omnidirectional sweep of the localized landscape that drastically accelerates fine-scale convergence speed and prevents premature local minima entrapment. The optimization performance of the proposed BSFA was rigorously benchmarked using 23 standard functions and the complex CEC2017 suite against ten powerful competing algorithms, including GA, PSO, GWO, LSHADE, BTA, and CAOA. Experimental and statistical analysis, verified via Wilcoxon non-parametric testing at a strict significance level of \(\:\alpha\:=0.05\) , demonstrates that BSFA achieves absolute global optimum values on key multimodal functions like TF9 and TF11, secures the lowest mean Friedman rank of 2.3 against its ablated variants, and yields competitive computational time metrics of 20.6 s across the entire test suite, ranking second in processing efficiency. These quantitative outcomes confirm that BSFA robustly eliminates suboptimal local valleys while drastically accelerating fine-scale convergence speed across diverse continuous optimization tasks.

title: PalmSpace: Towards a Versatile On-Palm Interaction Space through Unified Touch Modeling
abstract: As smart glasses and lightweight MR devices become increasingly practical, input remains a key challenge. The bare palm is an always-available, tactile, and proprioceptively accessible surface, but it has neither an explicit coordinate system nor embedded touch sensing. Prior on-palm systems typically expose isolated touch events, discrete regions, continuous trajectories, or task-specific gestures, limiting the palm's ability to support precise selection and gesture manipulation through a common input representation. We present PalmSpace, a wrist-worn infrared system that exposes mode-aware, body-referenced absolute input on the bare palm without per-user sensing calibration. At the interaction level, PalmSpace jointly represents contact occurrence, interaction mode, and palm-referenced absolute location; at the model level, it learns these coupled outputs through a shared real-time representation. In leave-one-participant-out evaluation with 17 participants, PalmSpace achieved 6.7 mm mean localization error, 98.9% contact detection accuracy, and 96.7% F1 for four-class interaction-state recognition. User studies further demonstrated absolute pointing and dragging, eyes-free digit input, and representative multi-finger controls including scrolling and pinch-based map manipulation. These results show that a morphologically variable bare palm can function as a transferable, mode-aware interaction surface.

title: From Global Alignment to Local Grounding: Zero-Shot Chinese Character Recognition with Radical Verification
abstract: Zero-shot Chinese character recognition (ZS-CCR) aims to recognize characters whose categories are never observed during training, and typically relies on the compositional structure shared between seen and unseen characters. Recent CLIP-style methods represent this structure with the Ideographic Description Sequence (IDS) and align it with glyph images in a shared embedding space. However, they rely on a single global image--IDS similarity that discards the spatial layout of radicals and, being learned only implicitly from seen classes, generalizes poorly to unseen ones; moreover, global matching often retrieves the correct character within the top candidates yet fails to rank it first when characters differ only in subtle local radicals. To address these issues, we propose a global-to-local two-stage framework. In the first stage, STG-CLIP augments the IDS with explicit tree-position and radical-level geometric priors, yielding a spatial-aware prototype that provides a consistent spatial description across seen and unseen categories for high-recall global retrieval. In the second stage, the Radical Verification Module (RVM) uses the radical instances of each retrieved candidate as queries to verify whether the corresponding radicals can be matched to spatially compatible regions in the input glyph. A margin-based gating rule activates the RVM only when the leading global candidates receive similar similarity scores. Experiments on the ICDAR2013 benchmark demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance under the character-level zero-shot setting, obtaining 83.06% top-1 accuracy with 2,755 seen classes. Ablation studies further show that the explicit geometric priors and radical-level verification provide complementary improvements.

title: QUTest: A Native Testing Framework for Quantum Programs
abstract: Quantum programs are often shared as OpenQASM 3 circuits, but tests are still written in host languages such as Python with Qiskit. We present QUTest, a native framework in which both programs and tests are standard .qasm files. Tests follow the Arrange / Act / Assert pattern, while configuration, runtime requirements, and assertions are encoded as pragma comments (//%), preserving compatibility with existing OpenQASM tools. QUTest provides 12 assertion types spanning deterministic, statistical, quantum-state, and structural checks, plus a linter and an environment-aware mode for running the same test across selected runtime versions in isolated environments. Its CLI supports automatic test discovery, runtime compatibility checks, and XML reports for continuous integration. We describe the pragma language, implementation, and a planned evaluation using coverage and mutation testing.

Tests follow the Arrange / Act / Assert pattern, while configuration, runtime requirements, and assertions are encoded as pragma comments (//%), preserving compatibility with existing OpenQASM tools. QUTest provides 12 assertion types spanning deterministic, statistical, quantum-state, and structural checks, plus a linter and an environment-aware mode for running the same test across selected runtime versions in isolated environments. Its CLI supports automatic test discovery, runtime compatibility checks, and XML reports for continuous integration. We describe the pragma language, implementation, and a planned evaluation using coverage and mutation testing.

title: A Lean 4 Formalization of a Discrete Core over Z/2^64 Z for Quantum-Style Computation and Reversible World Models
abstract: I present a small, layered Lean 4 library built on the finite ring Z/2^64 Z, whose arithmetic matches unsigned 64-bit machine arithmetic exactly. The base core defines an n-dimensional carrier with additive group and module structure, a structure-constant multiplication, an inner product, and a norm-preserving operator type. On this core we build a discrete quantum-style computation kernel (permutation and diagonal gates, circuits, tensor product) and a world-model layer (actions, observations, roll-outs, exact roll-back). The development formalizes that circuits and roll-outs preserve the norm, that the norm is multiplicative under the tensor product, and that reversible models can be rolled back exactly. The ring has zero divisors and no quantum advantage is claimed; the aim is an exact, reproducible, branch-free substrate with formally stated invariants for engineering use. A C++17 reference implementation and a test-vector generator are included for bit-exact cross-validation.

title: Defeating PCIe DMA & External Kernel Cheats through Usermode
abstract: Anti-cheat systems have spent a decade climbing into the kernel to detect external tools, yet cheats such as PCIe DMA devices run entirely outside the host CPU and read game state as plaintext. We argue the problem is not a lack of privilege but a lack of data secrecy. This paper presents a user-mode design that adapts Pointer Authentication Codes to x64 in software. Critical pointers are protected by a master key split across vector registers, a process-bound identity share, and a self-migrating heap share, so physical-memory readers recover only address-tethered ciphertext. Control-flow integrity checks, dual-pool shadow code verification, server-authoritative key rotation, and silent cryptographic poisoning raise the cost of internal and emulated attacks. On a test game, the hot path measures 300 to 500 cycles (median about 400), with early tuning pointing to about 140, and the cold path roughly 20,000 cycles (rounded median). The goal is not to make cheating impossible but to make it difficult and annoying enough to be impractical, and internal cheats can still bypass the current implementation with enough effort.

title: Construction and Application of Knowledge-Graph-Driven Smart Curriculum for General English
abstract: Against national digital-driven educational strategies, college English for non-English majors is troubled by fragmented resources, homogeneous teaching and limited personalized feedback. Targeting first-year non-English students, this study develops a knowledge-graph-enabled smart curriculum for General English. Combining top-down and bottom-up strategies, a two-tier knowledge graph is established: an ontology knowledge layer sorted from syllabus-centered five-skill knowledge points, and a data-resource layer built upon MOOC and SPOC resources on the Chaoxing Fanya platform. Based on a “teacher-student-machine” interactive framework, this paper presents the full-cycle teaching workflow covering pre-class guidance, in-class interaction and post-class adaptive push. Integrating ideological-political education and power-industry materials, this two-year research uses case studies. Pilot results show knowledge-graph visualization clarifies implicit links between language knowledge points, supports adaptive recommendation and multi-dimensional formative assessment. It offers feasible references for digital transformation of college foreign-language courses.

title: Toward Composable Intelligence: A Research Roadmap for Jev
abstract: Jev maps textual state to categorical choices, ordinal scores, and Boolean probabilities. We organize current methods and systems into four functional families. Experiments with TF–IDF, MiniLM, BM25, and a cross-encoder on BANKING77, CLINC150, and SciFact illustrate component interactions: improved in-domain calibration can accompany higher out-of-scope false acceptance, while greater candidate recall can coexist with lower observed ranking quality. We develop a roadmap for reusable decision programs that preserve the meaning of criteria, evidence, uncertainty, and action conditions as their components and tasks change.

title: Modular dual-critic reinforcement learning control for AUV path tracking and collision avoidance
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in complex and uncertain ocean environments require reliable path-tracking and obstacle-avoidance capabilities to maintain safety in the presence of currents and obstacles. Traditional end-to-end deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods often struggle with coupled navigation objectives, which can lead to oscillatory control and unreliable trajectory recovery. This paper proposes a modular dual-critic proximal policy optimization framework with prioritized experience replay (Modular DCPPO-PER) for AUV path tracking and collision avoidance. The framework separates navigation into two specialized policies for path tracking and collision avoidance and coordinates them through a time-to-collision-based soft risk arbitration mechanism. An actor-dual-critic-PER (ADCP) architecture is further introduced to improve learning stability and sample utilization by combining dual buffers with task-specific value estimation. In addition, a direction-sensitive reward function based on the sensor field of view assigns higher weights to high-risk perceptual regions and promotes smoother avoidance maneuvers. Simulation results in complex marine environments show that, compared with the advanced DRL baseline ARAB-PPO, the proposed method improves the average obstacle-avoidance success rate by 49.8% and reduces the path-tracking error by 12.9%. A USV-based physical surrogate experiment is also conducted to examine real-time inference, control continuity, and actuator-level feasibility on real hardware. The results indicate that the proposed framework can provide robust and smooth navigation behavior for AUV-oriented marine robotic applications, while full underwater AUV field validation remains future work.

title: Multi-modal feature fusion and classification of histopathological images using ensemble learning
abstract: Early and correct detection of cancer regions in histopathology images is important for timely diagnosis and treatment. In this work, we proposed a Explainable Artificial Intelligence based convolutional Neural network (CNN) framework for the classification of lung and colon cancer. The framework combines deep features from a CNN with hand-crafted features in a single hybrid feature pipeline. From each image, we first extract a 512-dimensional feature vector using a CNN. We then join this vector with 6084 HOG features and 10 LBP features to obtain a 6606-dimensional feature vector. To remove repeated and less useful information, we apply IPCA before training the models. On these reduced features, we train several classifiers: Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, and a custom MLP. Their predictions are then combined using a stacking-based ensemble so that the final model can use the strengths of each individual classifier. To make the system easier to understand for clinicians, we use SHAP-based explanation to show which features are important and how they affect the model output. The performance of the proposed ensemble framework is evaluated on LC25000 histopathology dataset and it obtains an accuracy of 99.38%, which is higher than several recent baseline methods. Furthermore, a detailed ablation study is performed to explain the role of each features extractor and combinations in precise classification. These finding concludes that combining deep and hand-crafted features with ensemble learning and simple explanation tools can lead to a reliable and accurate cancer classification system.

title: Rubric Spans are Label Representations: Joint LLM Encoding for Short Answer Scoring
abstract: Automatic Short Answer Scoring (ASAS) requires models that can score student responses against question-specific criteria while remaining efficient and transferable across rubric sets. We propose RUSPAN, a rubric-conditioned ASAS framework that treats rubric descriptions as semantic label representations. RUSPAN serialises the question context, student answer, and all candidate rubric levels into a single sequence, then scores the levels listwise from the rubric-span and whole-sequence representations produced in a single LM pass. We further introduce RUSPAN-RIM, in which a Rubric-Independent Mask prevents rubric spans from attending to one another, making rubric representations depend only on the answer and question context and preventing overfitting to rubric patterns during training for zero-shot transfer. On six ASAS benchmarks spanning English, German, and Portuguese, RUSPAN improves mono-benchmark scoring over discriminative and generative baselines, while RIM with position reindexing delivers consistent and substantial gains on PT-ASAG, the held-out benchmark with the strongest combined language and rubric-structure shift.

title: Predicted Futures Are Not Enough: Learning Executable Goals for Robot Manipulation
abstract: Generative world models provide rich predictions of how manipulation scenes may evolve toward task objectives, yet those futures do not directly expose the compact task variables required by control. When training supervises future prediction alone, terminal goal accuracy is not an explicit learning objective, even when geometric recovery is available. We present Entity-Level Goal Readout, a learned prediction-to-execution interface that makes the executable terminal goal an explicit output of a 3D trace world model. It combines object-centric pose prediction with translation grounded in observed depth to produce a compact goal in SE(3). A shared Pose-Native Executor consumes this fixed goal with online object-pose feedback for closed-loop control without rerunning the world model. Across five manipulation tasks, the pipeline achieves a mean success rate of 79.69%. Goal diagnostics directly measure terminal goal accuracy, while controlled translation perturbations characterize how execution degrades under goal error. Zero-shot deployment on a Franka arm achieves 73.33% success on nominal StackCube, 66.67% with distractors, and 75.00% on PickPlate with a target unseen during policy training. These results support treating the prediction-to-execution interface as an explicit learned component of world-model planning rather than incidental post-processing in the control pipeline itself. Project page: https://claire0730.github.io/executable-goals/

title: A variational quantum algorithm for nonlinear finite element analysis of hyperelastic materials
abstract: This manuscript explores a variational quantum formulation for nonlinear elasticity problems arising from hyperelastic material models. The approach leverages the potential energy structure of hyperelasticity and employs a hybrid quantum classical framework in which the energy functional is evaluated using parameterized quantum circuits and optimized through classical routines. To enable a hybrid (classical quantum implementation), polynomial approximations of the nonlinear terms in strain energy density are introduced, yielding a representation compatible with variational quantum algorithms. The methodology is demonstrated on a special case of the NeoHookean material model in a one dimensional setting using finite element discretizations with first and second order shape functions and nonhomogeneous boundary conditions. Numerical experiments investigate the influence of the polynomial approximation order on the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed approach, illustrating its feasibility for near-term quantum devices.

title: Certified Mathematical Growth of the Chrysene Formalism: Concordance Frontiers and Minimal Scission
abstract: We give a compact theory of certified extension for a formal presentation whose identity is constrained by an external reference structure. A protected fragment of an initial presentation is held fixed under ordinary extension, while mathematics outside that fragment may grow strictly. Candidate extensions carry proof provenance and are admitted only after passage of logically distinct mathematical, concordance, realization, and domain conditions. For a theorem with several proof routes, the inclusion-minimal sets of uncertified admission-requiring premises form a certification frontier. If ∅ ∉ Front_n(θ), then no recorded route supports assertoric certification; the corresponding frontier deficits instead yield conditional theorems. Provenance-labeled proof support prevents uncertified premises from acquiring certified status through intermediate derivations. Finally, a directed proof-support hypergraph and a least-fixed-point construction define theoretical scission: when previously certified support is invalidated, exactly the unsupported dependency region is removed while every theorem possessing a surviving grounded proof is retained. Applied to the Chrysene Formalism, the construction permits strict mathematical growth while preserving its Canonical Molecular Anchor.

title: Inteligencia artificial en la detección temprana del cáncer de laringe mediante análisis de imágenes endoscópicas
abstract: La inteligencia artificial aplicada a endoscopia laríngea muestra potencial para apoyar detección, clasificación y segmentación de lesiones. Se realizó una revisión narrativa crítica de estudios, metaanálisis y estándares de reporte. Se diferenciaron pacientes e imágenes, tareas diagnósticas y tipos de validación. Los resultados publicados muestran desempeño variable y experiencias de validación externa y vídeo, pero no acreditan por sí solos diagnóstico más temprano o mejores desenlaces oncológicos. Se propone una matriz de evaluación e implementación supervisada que integra calidad de datos, seguridad e impacto clínico. Se concluye que la adopción requiere validación independiente, control de sesgos y seguimiento de decisiones, manteniendo confirmación diagnóstica y responsabilidad especializada.

title: A Multi-Branch Framework for Multidimensional Online Review Analytics
abstract: Online product reviews combine unstructured narratives, star ratings, and helpfulness votes, but these signals answer different managerial questions and require different validation strategies. This study presents a reproducible multi-branch analytical framework for the Amazon Fine Food Reviews dataset (568,454 records; October 1999–October 2012). The framework includes exploratory text mining, LDA topic modeling, rating-derived polarity classification, structured-feature score prediction, and rule-based rating-helpfulness segmentation. To address sampling bias and leakage, the revised experiments use reproducible random sampling, product-grouped holdout sets, and feature estimation only on training data. LDA models with K = 3–8 were compared on a random sample of 20,000 reviews across three seeds; K = 3 showed the best held-out perplexity and the strongest topic stability among the tested solutions. For rating-derived polarity, class-weighted TF-IDF Logistic Regression achieved 94.55% accuracy, 94.04% balanced accuracy, 90.47% macro-F1, 93.29% negative recall, and 93.27% negative-class PR-AUC on an independent product-grouped test set (n = 104,282). A regression tree using structural review features outperformed a mean predictor but remained modest (MAE = 0.884, RMSE = 1.194, R2 = 0.175), limiting its use to exploratory analysis. Helpfulness analyses treated the 270,052 reviews with no votes as Unrated rather than NotHelpful. Sensitivity analysis across thresholds of 0.50–0.80 and minimum-vote requirements of 1, 2, 5, and 10 showed that the estimated Helpful share depends materially on both choices. The revised evidence therefore supports descriptive screening and hypothesis generation, not causal claims or autonomous managerial decisions. The contribution is a transparent comparison of complementary analytical branches under leakage-aware evaluation, together with explicit construct, sampling, and external-validity limits. The findings show why class-sensitive metrics, topic stability checks, independent test sets, and separate treatment of unexposed reviews are necessary before review analytics can inform practice.

title: LoRA based instruction fine tuning of large language models for agronomic triple extraction and GraphRAG knowledge retrieval
abstract: Abstract Due to massive growth in the unstructured agricultural data generated from reports, research articles, news, farmers' feedback, experts' advice etc, there is a need to utilize this information efficiently for knowledge representation and decision making. There are multiple techniques where information extraction and managing it in a structured manner can be less challenging. LLMs are used widely for extracting meaningful information in the way the user instructs. More precisely, LLMs when fine-tuned on domain-specific data e.g, agricultural data helps to retrieve information promptly. We propose a framework where the Llama model is fine-tuned using LoRA technique and instruction dataset for extracting triplets from the unstructured agronomic data. Further this Llama-LoRA-based model is used to generate knowledge which will efficiently help to retrieve the query results to user using GraphRAG. Domain specific instructional fine-tuning has shown significant rise in the performance. ROUGE-Precision and BLEU-precision results of the proposed framework has outperformed the response retrieval compared to other retrieval techniques. Proposed results of domain-specific instructional fine-tuned Llama-LoRA model has overcome the limitations of knowledge representation and unstructured data extraction through GraphRAG resulting in semantic search with contextual retrieval.

evidence.title: LoRA based instruction fine tuning of large language models for agronomic triple extraction and GraphRAG knowledge retrieval
evidence.abstract: Abstract Due to massive growth in the unstructured agricultural data generated from reports, research articles, news, farmers' feedback, experts' advice etc, there is a need to utilize this information efficiently for knowledge representation and decision making. There are multiple techniques where information extraction and managing it in a structured manner can be less challenging. LLMs are used widely for extracting meaningful information in the way the user instructs. More precisely, LLMs when fine-tuned on domain-specific data e.g, agricultural data helps to retrieve information promptly. We propose a framework where the Llama model is fine-tuned using LoRA technique and instruction dataset for extracting triplets from the unstructured agronomic data. Further this Llama-LoRA-based model is used to generate knowledge which will efficiently help to retrieve the query results to user using GraphRAG. Domain specific instructional fine-tuning has shown significant rise in the performance. ROUGE-Precision and BLEU-precision results of the proposed framework has outperformed the response retrieval compared to other retrieval techniques. Proposed results of domain-specific instructional fine-tuned Llama-LoRA model has overcome the limitations of knowledge representation and unstructured data extraction through GraphRAG resulting in semantic search with contextual retrieval.

title: Collusion-Secure Semi-Quantum Secret Sharing Scheme using a Quantum Third Party
abstract: The security of a secret sharing protocol is compromised if one or more dishonest participants can reconstruct the secret by deviating from the prescribed protocol, particularly when such malicious behavior remains undetected. Semi-Quantum Secret Sharing (SQSS) is a variant of secret sharing in which the participants possess only classical capabilities, such as preparing and measuring qubits in the computational ($Z$) basis, while a quantum-capable third party assists the dealer in generating and distributing quantum shares of a classical secret. The limited quantum capabilities of the participants in SQSS protocols may introduce vulnerabilities to collusion attacks, enabling an assisting quantum third party, in collaboration with a dishonest classical participant, to jointly recover the secret even without detection. In this work, we propose a novel SQSS protocol that eliminates this vulnerability and achieves information-theoretic security against collusion attacks. We further prove that the proposed protocol is secure against a broad class of external and internal attacks. Finally, a comparative analysis demonstrates that our construction advances existing SQSS protocols by simultaneously optimizing qubit efficiency, involves a classical dealer, and resilience against DCNA attacks using basic Bell states.

title: SANet: Selective Attention Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
abstract: Infrared small target detection aims to accurately identify and locate dim targets in complex backgrounds and supports applications such as maritime surveillance and military search and rescue. However, the small size and weak contrast of infrared targets make it difficult to balance detection accuracy and false alarms. This paper proposes a selective attention network (SANet) for infrared small target detection. A dual-path semantic-aware module combines standard and pinwheel-shaped convolutions to preserve local spatial consistency and capture broader contextual information. Spatial and channel attention further refine the features and improve target-background discrimination. To address the limitations of static skip connections in U-Net, a selective attention fusion module adaptively integrates features across scales using spatially varying weights. It selectively enhances salient regions and improves discrimination between true targets and false alarms. Experiments on three public benchmarks, NUAA-SIRST, IRSTD-1K, and NUDT-SIRST, show that SANet achieves competitive performance in intersection over union (IoU), normalized IoU, detection probability, and false alarm rate. Its IoU exceeds that of the second-best method by 1.93, 4.32, and 2.21 percentage points, respectively. These results support the effectiveness of SANet in dim-target perception, discriminative feature representation, and background suppression.

title: DSTNet: Dynamic Spectral Trajectory Network for Causal Multi-Horizon Financial Forecasting
abstract: Wavelet-based financial forecasters typically use the transform only to denoise, or reduce it to a single spectral snapshot at the forecast origin, and the convolution that produces the coefficients is usually bilateral, so it can read past the forecast origin. DSTNet instead retains the recent evolution of filter-bank magnitudes as a causal Dynamic Spectral Trajectory, built from seven trailing technical indicators over a twenty-day lookback with a one-sided Morlet-derived filter bank and an explicit burn-in for the left-boundary transient. A factorized Scale-Temporal Spectral Transformer attends along the time and filter-bank axes separately, a learned gate fuses the spectral branch with a CNN-BiLSTM, and horizon-specific gates emit one, three, five, and ten day forecasts in a single pass. We evaluate seven equity indices and gold under a common expanding-window protocol and an untouched one-year hold-out, against nine learned baselines and a random-walk persistence benchmark. Under MAE and MAPE, persistence is the strongest of the ten fixed competitors in 29 of the 32 series-horizon cells and DSTNet is the only model below it in every cell, by 0.7 to 0.9 percent at one day and 3.4 to 4.5 percent at ten days. At one day, paired testing favours DSTNet against the weaker learned baselines but is inconclusive against persistence and the strongest learned forecasters. A downstream allocation diagnostic does not support an equity-timing advantage on any of the seven indices.

title: LighTROcc: Lightweight 4D Occupancy Forecasting via Instance-Centric 3D Gaussians
abstract: Forecasting future 3D occupancy from surround-view cameras is essential for autonomous driving, yet existing approaches rely on dense voxel or bird's-eye-view representations whose cost grows rapidly with spatial resolution and prediction horizon. Because these representations do not explicitly maintain object identities, they also struggle to preserve instance consistency over time. We present LighTROcc, a lightweight instance-centric framework that represents movable objects with a compact set of learned queries and predicts present and future occupancy in a single forward pass. LighTROcc localizes each query through attention-guided forward lifting, combining image-space cross-attention, query-specific depth, and camera geometry to estimate its 3D center. Each instance is modeled as a mixture of anisotropic 3D Gaussians and propagated across future steps using predicted displacements, producing continuous, temporally consistent occupancy forecasts. Experiments on nuScenes and supplemented nuScenes-Occupancy show that LighTROcc outperforms the evaluated dense and instance-wise baselines in instance-level forecasting accuracy while maintaining strong voxel-level occupancy quality. Across different model configurations, LighTROcc achieves a favorable balance between forecasting accuracy and computational efficiency, demonstrating the potential of compact instance-centric modeling for camera-based 4D occupancy forecasting.

title: PROMPTECHO: A Pilot Study of Output Drift Under Developer-Style Prompt Variation
abstract: Studies of prompt sensitivity usually rewrite benchmark prompts with templates that the researchers designed. Developers rewrite prompts differently. They add background, split a request into steps, tighten a constraint, or ask for another output format. This paper is a small pilot on what those edits do to a model’s output. I define six categories of developer-style edits, build 24 pairs of prompts that ask for the same thing in two phrasings (12 code, 12 reasoning), and score each pair with a drift measure called PES, which runs from 0 (same behavior) to 1. For code, PES is the share of test inputs on which the two generated functions disagree. For reasoning, it compares final answers. Across 20 scored pairs, Claude Sonnet 5.5 averaged 0.063 and Phi-3-mini 0.131, and the interval for that gap includes zero. Nearly all of the drift came from pairs that add a constraint and from one pair on which Phi-3-mini answered the wrong question. Edits that only added context, steps, politeness, format instructions or a rephrasing produced no drift for Claude and one failure for Phi-3-mini. The sample is small and most pairs are authorwritten, so I treat the results as exploratory.GitHub Repository: https://github.com/Shriniketan369/PromptEcho

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Achieving Sustainable Development Goals in the ASEAN Region
abstract: The achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) across the ASEAN region is widely recognized to be significantly contributed to by the potential of artificial intelligence (AI). This study investigates how AI is being utilized to advance the social, economic, and environmental dimensions of the SDGs within ASEAN. It is suggested by the findings that various sectors, including manufacturing, education, agriculture, energy, and healthcare, are being transformed by AI, which drives innovation, improves efficiency, and promotes sustainability. However, obstacles to widespread AI adoption remain, such as gaps in digital infrastructure, workforce issues, and concerns regarding data privacy and displacement. This paper provides insights into the opportunities and barriers that ASEAN faces in leveraging AI for sustainable development, and recommendations for policy and strategy development are provided to maximize the benefits of AI while addressing these challenges. Finally, AI is an essential tool for environmental sustainability in ASEAN, particularly in managing energy consumption, optimizing renewable energy systems, and enhancing waste management. By facilitating smarter grids and optimizing energy production and consumption, AI is driving the transition to cleaner energy, thereby supporting SDG7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG13 (Climate Action).

title: Big Boxes, Not Black Boxes: What we can compute about LLMs, and what it may say about AGI
abstract: Deep networks are often thought of as black boxes. Their ability to encompass vast swathes of knowledge indeed makes them hard to explain. Yet many of their behaviours — generalization under overparametrization, grokking, OOD failures, neural scaling laws — recur across architectures and scales, and each, however surprising, can be reproduced and explained in controlled settings. I will review these efforts to identify and explain the universal phenomena of deep learning, and suggest that an LLM may amount to a sum of such tractable sub-phenomena, interpolative in nature. Finally, leaving scientific rigor aside, I'll argue that what separates this prosaic picture from the apparent magic of LLMs may well be the industrial scale of compute and human labour behind it, and that AGI in its deeper extrapolative sense may be much further away than claimed.

title: TE-SDNet: Temporally Enhanced Sequential Dependency Network for photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of photovoltaic (PV) power output is essential for ensuring the reliable and economic operation of grid-connected PV systems. However, due to the inherently strong fluctuations, pronounced periodicity, and the influence of various complex environmental factors on PV generation, existing time-based or variable-based forecasting models often fail to fully capture and exploit these characteristics. As a result, their accuracy and stability in PV power forecasting remain limited. To address these challenges, this paper proposes TE-SDNet, a three-component forecasting framework that efficiently exploits both temporal and variable-level information for short-term PV power prediction. The Temporal–Feature Decoupling Block (TFD) proposes a two-stage convolutional network to independently capture temporal dependencies and enrich feature representations. The Multi-Scale Temporal Mixing Block (MTM) introduces frequency-domain analysis to effectively identify salient periodic patterns and performs their decomposition and aggregation dynamically. In addition, the Inter-Variable Dependency Learning Block (IDL) is proposed to capture cross-variable correlations through a dedicated attention network operating along the variable dimension, enabling the framework to generate more accurate predictions. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, extensive experiments are conducted using data collected from fourteen PV plants located in two different regions of China. Averaged over two PV datasets and three forecasting horizons, TE-SDNet reduces RMSE by 2.2% and MAE by 3.1% relative to the strongest baseline, PatchTST, while requiring 94.6% fewer parameters and 99.6% fewer FLOPs. The source code of TE-SDNet is publicly available at https://github.com/Wokanood/TE-SDNet .

title: clflush-based Attacks on Modern Cloud Servers
abstract: Modern clouds usually rely on server CPUs, often deployed in multi-socket systems. Flush-based cache attacks have been extensively studied and leveraged, but mostly on single-socket systems, with client CPUs. In multi-socket servers, cache and memory latencies depend on the physical layout of cores, caches, and Numa nodes. Hence, system topology strongly influences the accuracy of such attacks. We thus investigate the impact of this growing complexity on the effectiveness of such attacks. We present a large-scale, topology-aware study of Flush+Reload and Flush+Flush across 36 single- and multi-socket Intel and AMD servers. We show topology-induced contributions dominate the latency variations. Notably, Numa ’s contribution on multi-socket systems makes topology-unaware attacks unreliable. Our topology-aware calibration accounts for such parameters as attacker/victim cores, memory Numa node, and target address, improving error rates and attack viability. We show Flush+Flush applies widely to AMD CPUs, and is often more accurate than Flush+Reload on modern x86 targets. Lastly, we introduce Load/Flush+Reload , a covert-channel that compares invalid loads to shared loads, with twice the true capacity of Flush+Reload /Flush+Flush . Our results show that topology awareness is required for reliable cache attacks on recent platforms, and provide practical guidance for attackers and defenders.

title: Whose Ground Truth? Embracing Ambiguity in Human-Centered AI
abstract: As AI systems increasingly interact with people and make decisions about them, understanding human interpretations becomes an important part of developing human-centered AI. Conventional machine learning and AI systems are largely developed under the assumption that a single definitive ground truth exists, with variability in human annotations often resolved through aggregation or treated as noise. However, for many human-centered tasks, human interpretation is inherently ambiguous, and multiple interpretations of the same input may be simultaneously reasonable and valid. Reducing such ambiguity to a single target risks overlooking meaningful information about the diversity of human perception, judgment, and experience. In this position paper, we call for a shift towards modeling the interpretation space of plausible human judgments, while distinguishing meaningful ambiguity from annotation noise. We argue that this perspective should guide how AI systems are represented, learned, evaluated, deployed, and governed, supporting more human-centered AI that better reflects the diversity of human interpretation.

title: Koopman Observers for Diffusion Acceleration: Correcting Feature Forecasts with Shallow Measurements
abstract: Feature caching accelerates diffusion sampling by replacing expensive network evaluations with predictions from previously computed activations. However, forecasts based only on past features cannot directly incorporate changes in the current denoising state. We investigate whether inexpensive, freshly computed features can serve as observations for correcting these predictions. We introduce an observation-corrected Koopman framework for accelerating frozen diffusion models. Using calibration trajectories, we identify finite-dimensional, time-dependent Koopman approximations that jointly describe the increments of shallow and deep network features. During accelerated sampling, these operators predict the evolution of expensive deep features, while innovations in the observed shallow features correct the predicted state. Periodic full evaluations refresh the observer, and all generative-model parameters remain unchanged. This formulation enables controlled comparisons of temporal prediction and observation correction. Across three 10,000-image runs per dataset, our method reduces paired Inception-feature MSE by $19.9\%$ on CIFAR-10 and $11.9\%$ on a ten-class ImageNet subset relative to channelwise affine prediction under the same four-partial-step schedule. Matched ablations attribute additional reductions of $4.54\%$ and $4.67\%$ to observation correction. The observer achieves $1.89\times$ and $1.85\times$ measured speedups over DDIM-50, supporting improved reference-sampler fidelity without retraining the denoiser.
