title: IA para representantes comerciais
abstract: IA para representantes comerciais apresenta um percurso de aplicação de inteligência artificial para representantes, distribuidores e vendedores externos.O objetivo do livro é ajudar o leitor a aumentar a produtividade da carteira com preparação de visita e acompanhamento contextualizado. O conteúdo usa casos didáticos fictícios, exemplos e propostas de trabalho para discutir decisões, organização de informações e revisão humana.Ao longo dos 10 capítulos, você encontrará:Resultado da carteira comercialCatálogo e condiçõesHistórico e preparaçãoBriefing de visita com IAComparativos e propostasO percurso avança até Projeto: uma semana de visitas preparada. title: The Morrison Invariant-Governed Evolution Framework A Unified Formalism for Preserved Structure, Admissible Change, Authority, Commit, and Return
abstract: Thispapersynthesizesamulti-stageresearchprogrammedevelopedacrossgovernedadaptation, invariant preservation, field-theoretic identity dynamics, nilpotent governance, MIFT, TENGEN, and causal correction. The unifying object is an invariant-governed transition system in which candidate generation, admissibility, authorization, state commit, and retrospective repair are mathematically distinct operations. A state space is decomposed into protected and adaptive structure, candidatetransitionsaregeneratedwithoutintrinsicauthority, admissibilityisevaluated against stated invariants, authorization is represented independently where required, and commit occurs only after the relevant conditions are satisfied. The framework yields a master invariant- preservation theorem, a non-commit theorem for rejected transitions, a TENGEN specialization formalizing COPY ̸= COMMIT, and a conditional return/repair formulation for correcting invalid causal transitions without indiscriminate erasure. The synthesis also clarifies an important separation of evidential levels: proving the abstract governance architecture does not by itself validate any particular physical interpretation, cryptographic primitive, geometric constant, or implementation. The result is intended as a compact formal backbone for a broader corpus whose historical lineage begins in publicly documented gated-evolution work and later develops through MIFT, governed AI commit boundaries, TENGEN authorization separation, and RETURN WITHOUT ERASURE.

title: Exascale Quantum & Molecular Simulation
abstract: Abstract This computational verification Lean4 module parameterizes diffeomorphic structures over an arbitrary field `K` (`[Field K]`) and an arbitrary finite indexing type `ι` (`[Fintype ι]`), thus, we lift the entire framework out of real analysis into pure, abstract linear algebra and module theory. Physicists simulate quantum molecular dynamics or quantum field interactions on classical computers, they are forced to truncate the infinite Hilbert space to a finite basis, iota. Standard wisdom says this truncation always discards high-frequency tails, introducing systematic truncation errors. A generalized_observable_dot_product_reduction proves that if the target observable v belongs to the invariant subspace V = ext{span}\_K{f\_alpha}, its continuous field value v(u^\*) collapses exactly to a finite complex dot product \\langle c, z angle. Combined with `generalized_generator_action_as_matrix_multiplication`, the time evolution of the continuous quantum state operator (G^\* f\_alpha)(u^\*) maps without error onto the finite complex matrix update (L z)\_alpha. Further, as the matrix reduction 'theorem_generalized_generator_action_as_matrix_multiplication' proves that evaluating the non-linear state transformation (G^* f_alpha)(u^*) is identically equal to the finite matrix-vector product (L z)_alpha over F_q. Because the state update function G^\* satisfies `ExactTruncationCriterion` inside the bijectively separated rank coordinate space A(\\mathbf{P}), the non-linear trapdoor is bypassed. Reversing a round or finding a pre-image reduces to solving a system of linear equations L z = b over F_q. This is a Theta(m) linear matrix retrieval on classical hardware. With gratitude to all of mathematics, Dr. Charles Tibedo

title: Dynamic Topology-Preserving Multi-Label Class-Incremental Learning
abstract: To address the insufficient stability of the feature space in class-incremental learning, this paper proposes a Dynamic Topology-Preserving Multi-Label Class-Incremental Learning (DTP-MLCIL) method. Specifically, a Neural Gas (NG) network is introduced to construct and maintain an adaptive topological skeleton of the feature space through the Competitive Hebbian Learning (CHL) algorithm, thereby approximating and tracking the underlying feature distribution at the manifold geometry level. Based on this topological representation, an anti-forgetting node loss is designed to constrain the consistency between current features and the historical topology from both node-position and topological-connectivity perspectives, thereby reinforcing regions that encode previously acquired knowledge. Furthermore, a max-min loss is introduced to proactively organize the feature space of newly emerging classes, encouraging new class representations to remain well separated from historical regions while forming compact intra-class clusters. By explicitly preserving the geometric stability of the feature space, the proposed method effectively alleviates structural drift and topological distortion during the incremental learning process. Comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: VICO: Visual Environments Co-Evolving for Vision-Language Model Reasoning
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a standard recipe for post-training vision-language models (VLMs), but it typically assumes a static training environment. As the actor improves, fixed tasks drift out of its learning frontier: many become trivial, others remain unsolvable; and the learning signal collapses. We argue that VLM post-training should evolve the visual environment alongside the actor, not just the actor itself. We propose VICO, a co-evolutionary framework in which an actor and an Environment-as-Rewriter (EnvRewriter) are trained jointly: the EnvRewriter edits verifiable image-side structures, such as scene graphs, chart tables, or protected region masks, and re-renders them to produce label-valid training samples whose difficulty is calibrated to the actor's current ability through a pass-rate-based reward. This loop continuously realigns task difficulty with actor capability without any additional human annotation. Across nine multimodal benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning and visually grounded understanding, VICO-8B improves over its base model by up to +5.0% on out-of-domain tasks, surpasses the strongest self-evolution and text-editing co-evolution baselines by +4.3% and +8.4% respectively, and stays comparable to chart-specialized RLVR methods using 16-160 times fewer labeled samples. By shifting from human-labeled supervision to image-editing co-evolution, VICO offers a scalable path beyond static-corpus RLVR for visual reasoning.

title: Safe Learning of Adaptive Control Policies for Remote Patient Monitoring
abstract: Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) enables continuous observation of patients in their daily environments, improving both health outcomes and quality of life. A key challenge in RPM is determining the optimal monitoring intensity, while balancing patient safety and monitoring costs. This problem is further complicated when system parameters, such as transition probabilities and costs, are initially unknown. We develop a learning-based control framework that estimates these parameters and adapts the monitoring policy in real time. The proposed approach is an online model-based reinforcement learning algorithm tailored to RPM, with patient safety explicitly prioritized during exploration. We provide theoretical guarantees on safety and convergence to the optimal policy. Simulation results show that the algorithm converges to the optimal threshold-based policy, maintains low treatment costs, and reduces the risk of patients reaching critical health states.

title: Agent4RE: A Self-Refining Multi-agent Framework for End-to-End Software Requirements Engineering and Benchmarking
abstract: Existing LLM-based approaches for software Requirements Engineering (RE) typically rely on basic prompting strategies or rudimentary agent collaboration, under-utilizing the full potential of multi-agent systems. Meanwhile, available datasets focus on isolated subtasks, such as requirements extraction, classification, and completeness detection, leaving the absence of an end-to-end RE benchmark that spans from requirements elicitation to generation. We present Agent4RE - a self-refining multi-agent RE system that orchestrates specialized agents and incorporates two iterative improvement loops. To support evaluation, we construct RE-E2E - a real-world dataset built from human-written requirement specifications, enabling end-to-end assessment of RE workflows. Building on this foundation, we further propose two enhanced Agent4RE versions that incorporate either autonomous self-refinement or structured human feedback, and analyze their strengths and limitations across different scenarios. Evaluation on 8 Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrates that all three Agent4RE variants consistently outperform a domain-context-augmented prompting baseline by average 8% in text-based metrics. The two enhanced variants achieve the highest LLM-as-a-judge and human ratings, surpassing two RE baselines by approximately 0.8 points on a four-point scale. This consistent performance establishes Agent4RE as a practical end-to-end RE solution for industrial environments.

title: An effective macroscopic description of early-stage chemical equilibration in high-energy heavy-ion collisions
abstract: The early stage of high-energy heavy-ion collisions undergoes transient dynamics, evolving non-perturbatively from a gluon-rich to a chemically equilibrated quark-gluon plasma. We develop an effective hydrodynamic approach that casts the microscopic quark equilibration dynamics as the relaxation evolution of an effective macroscopic bulk viscous pressure. The evolution of this effective bulk viscous pressure captures quark chemical equilibration and the breaking of conformal symmetry, thereby providing a smooth onset of the lattice QCD equation of state after a few fm/c in the hydrodynamic evolution. We investigate phenomenological effects of this macroscopic description on final-state observables in Pb+Pb, O+O, and p+Pb collisions at the Large Hadron Collider.

title: Building codes with transversal CCZ using projective geometry and SAT solvers
abstract: We construct CSS codes with three logical qubits whose logical CCZ gate is implemented by transversal physical $T/T^{\dagger}$ gates and whose distance is at least $3$. These codes start with $8$-divisible $X$-stabilizers defined by projective geometry, which guarantees $d_Z\geq 3$. A SAT solver then finds three $X$-logical operators compatible with the transversal CCZ. We build codes at thirteen block lengths from $n=48$ to $n=496$, with $d_Z=3$ or $4$, and illustrate the method with the $[[48,3,3]]$ code $Q_{48}$. Additionally, we prove that no CSS code with three logical qubits, $Z$-distance at least $3$, and a quasi-transversal CCZ gate (transversal $T$ with a diagonal Clifford correction) exists below $n=39$. The $[[47,3,3]]$ code of Jacinto et al. serves as an upper bound, leaving $39\leq n\leq46$ open.

title: Game theory driven multi-agent framework mitigates language model hallucination
abstract: Lightweight large language models hold promise for scientific applications but remain limited in rule-constrained domains because they can reproduce linguistic patterns without following scientific principles, leading to hallucinations. Here, we show that G-Frame, an adaptive multi-agent framework inspired by Bayesian game and team game principles, enables a closed-loop process for automated data generation, model evaluation, and training. By assigning complementary roles to multiple agents, G-Frame generates structured reasoning data and constructs a specialized corpus containing 363,045 chain-of-thought examples and 199,589 question–answer pairs. Using this corpus together with domain pre-training and adaptive training, the 7-billion-parameter model OmniChem achieves competitive performance across the reported benchmarks and reduces the ChemJudge hallucination rate from 41.95% for the base model to 12.91%. Case studies further illustrate potential applications in molecular design and selected synthesis-planning tasks. These results support G-Frame as an extensible game theory-driven multi-agent framework for improving the reliability of lightweight scientific language models. Lightweight AI models can be unreliable in specialized scientific tasks. Here, the authors introduce G-Frame, which uses game theory to coordinate multiple AI agents, automate data generation and training, and reduce hallucinations.

evidence.title: Game theory driven multi-agent framework mitigates language model hallucination
evidence.abstract: Lightweight large language models hold promise for scientific applications but remain limited in rule-constrained domains because they can reproduce linguistic patterns without following scientific principles, leading to hallucinations. Here, we show that G-Frame, an adaptive multi-agent framework inspired by Bayesian game and team game principles, enables a closed-loop process for automated data generation, model evaluation, and training. By assigning complementary roles to multiple agents, G-Frame generates structured reasoning data and constructs a specialized corpus containing 363,045 chain-of-thought examples and 199,589 question–answer pairs. Using this corpus together with domain pre-training and adaptive training, the 7-billion-parameter model OmniChem achieves competitive performance across the reported benchmarks and reduces the ChemJudge hallucination rate from 41.95% for the base model to 12.91%. Case studies further illustrate potential applications in molecular design and selected synthesis-planning tasks. These results support G-Frame as an extensible game theory-driven multi-agent framework for improving the reliability of lightweight scientific language models. Lightweight AI models can be unreliable in specialized scientific tasks. Here, the authors introduce G-Frame, which uses game theory to coordinate multiple AI agents, automate data generation and training, and reduce hallucinations.

title: agloss: code and results for "Guidance versus Confinement: What Anatomical Supervision of Grad-CAM Does and Does Not Change"
abstract: PyTorch code and result files for the manuscript Guidance versus Confinement: What Anatomical Supervision of Grad-CAM Does and Does Not Change (under review). The package agloss trains tuberculosis chest X-ray classifiers (ResNet-50, ConvNeXt-Tiny) with and without spatial supervision of Grad-CAM: anatomical guidance (the Anatomical Guidance loss), anatomical confinement (Tversky), and their ablations. It runs the full experiment grid (336 training runs: two datasets, eight seeds), the cross-dataset transfer evaluation, and the reliance analyses (occlusion, region ablation, deletion-insertion). Two commands reproduce every experiment; the included result CSVs reproduce every table and figure without a GPU. The Shenzhen and Montgomery County datasets and the Shenzhen lung masks are not included; they are publicly available from the U.S. National Library of Medicine and Kaggle (see README).

title: Artificial Intelligence as an Investment Case
abstract: Artificial intelligence expands what businesses can earn and can accelerate how quickly they earn it. My investment view begins with a rising frontier: exceptional performance becomes harder to sustain, yet the tools, effective research effort, and organizational capacity used to reach the next threshold can improve even faster. The opportunity is not only cheaper existing work. It includes previously uneconomic activities, faster experimentation, new products, and earlier cash flows. This manuscript develops that affirmative thesis across infrastructure, models, applications, scientific discovery, and established operating businesses. It connects customer value to defensible market share, net income, reinvestment, and cash per share. A transparent 2030 reference screen gives approximately \$5.62 trillion of annual gross AI-related vendor revenue and \$1.05 trillion of net-income capacity. These are conditional screening quantities, not consolidated final demand or incremental global profit. Dynamic margin compression lowers modeled income to approximately \$789 billion on the same revenue path; a separate, assumption-dependent capital-renewal overlay gives approximately \$686 billion. Asset-vintage schedules, matched software and logistics counterfactuals, zero-profit model scenarios, and the value of faster learning expose the mechanisms behind those outcomes. Leopold Aschenbrenner's \textit{Situational Awareness} supplies a consequential research-automation scenario, not a mandatory timetable or a substitute for financial analysis. The conclusion is constructive and selective: invest in businesses that repeatedly convert improving intelligence into valuable paid activity, retain a differentiated role when intelligence becomes cheaper, and generate cash after financing their next advance.

title: What Persists Matters More Than What Changes
abstract: A reusable world model need not reproduce every future observation exactly. What matters is which distinctions remain stable when forecasts, tasks, or trained instances change. Independently trained models may give different values yet preserve the same relation among matched intervention consequences. This motivates separating state from coordinates and dynamics from realized paths. The same view separates reachability from preference and stable relations from numerical values. Reachability captures possible futures, while persistence tests which relations chosen before evaluation remain stable across selected variations. A smooth deterministic system provides one precise setting, but the underlying perspective is not tied to an explicit model. It also applies to predictive structure embedded in a policy or used in a hybrid system. Persistence itself needs no shared latent coordinates or invariant latent manifold. These distinctions clarify what may change, what should persist, and what evidence supports the claim.

title: The Handover Problem: Governing Autonomy Transitions in Human-AI Collaboration
abstract: Human-machine systems rarely operate at a fixed level of AI autonomy. As operators and AI systems collaborate over time, control must shift: the AI can take on more responsibility when collaboration is stable, maintain its current role when evidence is ambiguous, or return control to the human when conditions deteriorate. Existing work on adaptive automation, supervisory control, trust in automation, and deskilling explains parts of this problem, but provides no auditable, multi-signal criterion for governing when autonomy should change across multi-cycle workflows. We formalise this challenge as the Handover Problem: deciding, at each operational cycle, whether to escalate, maintain, or revert AI autonomy while keeping the process reversible, recoverable, and auditable. We introduce the Handover Readiness Score (HRS), a transparent composite measure that integrates four signal dimensions: operator readiness, human-AI trust, learning stability, and operational performance. It is combined with a hysteresis-based transition policy that requires sustained positive evidence before increasing autonomy but reverts promptly when conditions worsen. Across software engineering and manufacturing domains, the HRS and hard safety guards address complementary failure regimes: guards enforce immediate corrective action when a single indicator breaches a critical threshold, while the HRS detects the slow, multi-signal erosion of operator readiness that no individual guard can observe. The framework establishes autonomy handover as a governance problem requiring explicit, composite, and auditable criteria. This provides a conceptual and formal foundation that adaptive automation research has not previously provided.

title: Progress and Prospect of AI in ARPES Workflow
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an increasingly useful tool across the experimental sciences, including angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), which routinely produces large, multidimensional datasets of electronic structure. Recent advances in AI and machine learning (ML) have opened new opportunities across the entire ARPES workflow, from automated sample preparation and real-time data acquisition to post-experiment data analysis and comparison with theoretical calculations. Despite this progress, a comprehensive review of ML applications, their capabilities, and reliability across the different stages of ARPES workflow is still lacking. In this review, we first introduce ML methods that are most relevant to experimentalists working in condensed matter physics and materials science. We then follow the ARPES workflow, reviewing existing ML applications at each step and discussing their advantages, limitations and potential for future development. We also examine the current ARPES data landscape, where several open databases are available but remain relatively small and fragmented compared with large, shared datasets such as ImageNet. Given these limitations, we suggest that the community focus on sharing pretrained models that can be further trained, adapted to specific tasks, and redistributed, while working toward a larger and standardized open ARPES dataset repository. Finally, we discuss our perspectives on the future of AI within the ARPES workflow using a six-level framework of laboratory automation, highlighting the opportunities and challenges in moving toward a fully autonomous, self-driving ARPES laboratory.

title: Tradeoff between Wigner negativity and decoherence time for cubic Gaussian states
abstract: Wigner negativity has been shown to be a resource in quantum computing, raising the question of how to efficiently produce states with a large Wigner negativity. Cubic Gaussian states, obtained when a cubic gate is applied to a Gaussian state, have been proposed as candidates for this purpose. We show that cubic Gaussian states with a large Wigner negativity $\mathcal N$ necessarily have a short decoherence time $τ$ that is bounded above by $\mathcal N^{-2}$. In other words, a large Wigner negativity comes at a cost: the decoherence time $τ$ of cubic Gaussian states decreases at least quadratically in the negativity $\mathcal N$. Maximizing $τ$ at fixed Wigner negativity $\mathcal N$, we show that this upper bound is reached by optimal cubic Gaussian states. They have the property that for large negativity, the optimal squeezing scales as $\ln\mathcal N$ and the optimal cubicity as $\mathcal N^{-1}$. Optimal cubic Gaussian states with large negativity can therefore be constructed with small cubicity, provided sufficient squeezing is applied. However, their decoherence time decreases with growing negativity. In addition, we show that their preparation is extremely sensitive to thermal noise. Finally, we compare, for each integer $n$, the optimal cubic Gaussian state with the $n$th Fock state that has the same negativity: despite their pronounced differences in photon number distribution and Wigner function, we show that they have similar, be it slightly larger, decoherence times and entanglement generating potential through a beam splitter.

title: Constrained Hebbian learning supports efficient representational allocation under structural constraints
abstract: Introduction Biological systems are constrained by anatomy and metabolism, with synaptic maintenance consuming substantial energy and spatial limitations restricting connectivity. These constraints favor neural codes that compress behaviorally relevant information into low-redundancy patterns. Here, we investigate whether an excitatory competitive Hebbian rule can implement synaptic resource allocation under anatomical and metabolic constraints, and whether the resulting representations occupy a more favorable cost-performance regime than reference learning rules. Methods Representational cost is operationalized using mutual-information-based quantities derived from the Variational Information Bottleneck objective. Experiments employ three audiovisual benchmarks (AVE, Kinetics-Sounds, and VGGSound100) with fixed upstream audiovisual embeddings as a controlled higher-level sensory regime. We isolate downstream associative plasticity and compare Hebbian learning against biologically inspired local target-propagation (DDTP) and backpropagation (BP) under matched sparsity and architectural constraints. Results Hebbian learning yields lower task-information cost CTI than sparse BP- and DDTP-trained networks in the main compressed comparisons, while reaching a CTI range comparable to shallow nonnegativity-constrained BP. Rather than uniformly improving classification performance, Hebbian learning shifts the trade-off between task-relevant information and representational cost, yielding lower CTI at comparable functional performance in several settings. Discussion Overall, the results indicate an explicit cost-performance trade-off rather than uniform accuracy gains, while maintaining functional task performance under the evaluated constraints. For a given level of task-relevant information, less information about the input is retained; task performance remains functional, although it can be slightly reduced on some datasets. These results support a computational-neuroscientific interpretation of Hebbian learning as a local mechanism for synaptic resource allocation, rather than as a general-purpose strategy for maximizing audiovisual classification accuracy.

title: Cosine Is Not Semantics: Learning a Spectral Metric from the Embedding Corpus as alternative approach
abstract: Cosine similarity is widely used as a proxy for semantic similarity between embeddings but its semantic interpretation depends on the representation and training objective rather than on the normalized inner product itself. We study a corpus-conditioned alternative: a graph over embedding features supplies a positive-semidefinite operator that changes the geometry in which angular agreement is measured. The resulting normalized spectral kernel (the spectral blend) compares graph gradients of embedding signals, admits an explicit feature map, and recovers ordinary cosine under the identity operator. We establish its kernel properties, characterize the information discarded by the Laplacian nullspace and describe a regularized extension and a non-negative spectral-filter family. The pairwise kernel is kept separate from scalar spectral-energy read-outs. We describe eugenio, a Rust implementation that realizes the kernel through an explicit cut-invariant feature map, and specify an evaluation protocol based on independent semantic judgments, relevance labels, and graph-randomization controls. The operator is estimated from the corpus and then fixed; no end-to-end optimization is involved. This draft establishes the mathematical construction and its implementation contract; whether the resulting geometry improves semantic alignment remains an empirical question.

title: ASM-EA: Reproducibility Artifact for "A Surrogate-Assisted Multi-mode Algorithm with Constraint Boundary Awareness for Tightly Constrained Expensive Optimization"
abstract: Reproducibility artifact for ASM-EA, a surrogate-assisted multi-mode evolutionary algorithm with constraint boundary awareness for tightly constrained expensive optimization. The archive contains everything needed to rebuild the experimental environment and reproduce all reported results. Contents code/ — full source code: ASM-EA and baselines (SACCDE, GLoSADE, DE), Kriging surrogate with uncertainty, benchmark suites (CEC2006, CEC2010, CEC2017, engineering benchmarks, IEEE 30-bus carbon-constrained ED), and stage-by-stage experiment runners (baseline, full comparison, ablation, sensitivity, case studies, publication figures). environment/ — exact environment specification: pinned dependency lock file (requirements.lock.txt), requirements.txt, Conda environment.yml, and setup notes (Python 3.9). data/ — re-run experiment results backing the manuscript tables and figures. figures/ — publication figures in vector PDF and 600-DPI PNG. README.md — archive overview and reproduction instructions. Requirements: Python 3.9 with the pinned dependencies in environment/requirements.lock.txt (NumPy 2.0, SciPy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, pandas, joblib). CPU only; no GPU required.

title: From Cognitive Overload to Individualized Learning: AI Tutoring in Electrical Engineering
abstract: First-year students in electrical engineering often encounter significant challenges in their undergraduate programs, particularly due to heterogeneous prior knowledge in mathematics and physics, as well as difficulties in managing their own learning processes. These issues frequently result in cognitive overload, poor exam performance, and high dropout rates. Traditional teaching methods, especially in large cohorts, struggle to address these challenges effectively, as excessive tutorial time is spent on basic calculation steps rather than fostering deeper, subject-specific understanding. To address this, a domain-specific AI tutor was piloted during the winter semester of 2025/2026 in the first-semester course "Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering". The AI, based on the Google Gemini 2.5 Pro language model, was enhanced with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to integrate tailored teaching materials, such as annotated lecture transcripts and detailed solution manuals. Configured as a Socratic tutor, the AI provided individualized, asynchronous support by guiding students through tutorial preparation, verifying their calculation steps, and assisting with step-by-step troubleshooting. This tool was tested with a seminar group of 18 students who got access to the AI tutor via the platform you.com. The pilot project included continuous data collection throughout the semester. Weekly online reflection forms captured students' usage patterns, perceived task difficulty, and feedback on the AI's usefulness or limitations. These data were complemented by two comprehensive surveys conducted at midterm and end of semester. The study presents the technological configuration and didactic applications of the AI tutor, analyzing its impact across different student performance levels. The results indicate high acceptance of the AI tutor, particularly for verifying calculations and resolving short-term learning obstacles. However, the analysis also revealed limitations, especially in handling subject-specific visual and topological contexts. The findings underscore the importance of fostering critical AI literacy among students and highlight the need for future multimodal AI models to better support engineering education. In addition, the use of AI in undergraduate studies serves to build competencies within the context of a potential core curriculum.

title: VQMedNet NISQ aware quantum feature embedding with QFeatEmbed VQC for MRI and CT disease diagnosis
authors: Grandhi V. V. S. R. Krishna
abstract: Although automated diagnosis in medical imaging has made tremendous breakthroughs with deep learning, current models also exhibit difficulties with representation stability, calibration, and robustness to domain heterogeneity. Traditional methods that use deeper CNN or transformer networks incur greater computational costs without fully addressing feature separability and uncertainty estimation. To address these shortcomings, the present study proposes a hybrid quantum-classical approach, VQMedNet, that integrates variational quantum circuits with classical feature extraction for supervised classification of MRI and CT images. The suggested QFeatEmbed-VQC module is an NISQ-conscious nonlinear quantum feature embedding that can be trained on tokenised and compressed image features, enabling effective learning with constrained quantum resources. A gradual training approach is followed to achieve consistent optimisation, and calibration-sensitive assessment is included to measure the predictability. The experiments with the brain tumour MRI (BraTS) and lung CT (LIDC-IDRI) datasets show a stable increase over the classical baseline, achieving 95.6% accuracy and 0.947 Macro-F1 on MRI classification, and 93.1% accuracy with improved AUC-PR on CT tasks. Additional analyses show enhanced embedding separability, robustness to domain perturbations, and reduced Expected Calibration Error. Moreover, the findings suggest that moderate-depth quantum circuits offer a good balance between performance and computational complexity. Although tested under simulation-based conditions, the proposed framework can indicate the potential of quantum-enhanced feature embedding for building stable and efficient medical AI systems. It may be seen as a promising approach to future NISQ-aware diagnostics. The implementation is publicly available at: https://github.com/gvvsrk/QuantumMed-FedDx . Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

title: NEMORA: Neural Equivariant Multipole Operators for Long-Range Atomistic Learning
abstract: Equivariant graph neural networks have emerged as foundational architectures for machine-learned interatomic potentials, approaching quantum-chemical accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. These models describe local atomic environments accurately, but finite spatial cutoffs truncate long-range information flow, and stacking message-passing layers can lead to over-smoothing and over-squashing. Existing long-range extensions either prescribe a fixed analytical propagation kernel, restrict long-range communication to scalars or degree-preserving channels, are only approximately equivariant, or incur super-linear computational cost. Combining learnable long-range equivariant transport with multiscale many-body expressivity and efficient scaling for larger systems remains a central challenge. We introduce Neural Equivariant Multipole Operators (NEMORA), a neural equivariant extension of the Fast Multipole Method (FMM) for learning long-range tensorial representations. NEMORA generalizes the FMM's analytical multipole expansion and translation operators to learned equivariant counterparts on an adaptive spatial hierarchy. Its operators couple angular degrees and form many-body interactions across length scales, retaining the FMM's hierarchical organization and analytical radial factors as physical inductive biases while learning data-dependent long-range couplings. NEMORA evaluates in linear time and memory complexity, allowing it to treat larger systems than other long-range methods reaching hundreds of thousands of atoms, and it augments both symmetry-constrained and unconstrained short-range backbones. On non-local benchmarks, it reduces force and energy errors relative to the short-range backbones by over an order of magnitude and up to three orders of magnitude, respectively, which is better than or competitive with existing long-range extensions in accuracy.

title: Tracing Inputs, Verifying Outputs: Validating Attribution in Music Generation
abstract: How can we verify whose music contributed to an AI-generated output? This paper demonstrates how input-based attribution can provide verifiable evidence of which audio sources were used in a generation and whether they shaped the output. To do so, we condition the generation solely on audio without any text input, then trace the inputs behind each output, and establish their musical effect. In prompt adherence tests and controlled input swaps, the stems generated by our generator, MixAudio, follow the prompt audio in timbre and the context audio in harmony. Yet these outputs may still reproduce training data not supplied as inputs. We therefore audit memorization with our musical version identification model, musicDNA, and find few reproductions outside the input records. On human-judged cases within the flagged pool, it achieves higher precision and recall than the other tested memorization detectors. The two evaluations suggest that input records and output analysis provide complementary evidence for attribution, on which rights-holder reporting and compensation can draw as the AI music economy takes shape. Audio examples are available at https://neutune.github.io/attr2027demo/

title: BARE-AI: Bit-Flip Attack Resilience in AI Hardware through Built-in Performance Monitors
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are integral to many safety critical systems, yet they remain highly vulnerable to bit-flip attacks (BFAs), where a few memory level perturbations can drastically degrade accuracy. Existing defenses incur significant hardware overhead, depend on retraining, or fail against targeted flips. We propose BARE-AI, a runtime framework that detects, localizes, and mitigates BFAs during inference. BARE-AI introduces AI Performance Counters (APCs), lightweight hardware monitors in the accelerator datapath that capture per-layer activation statistics such as sparsity, entropy, kurtosis, and spectral shift. These are analyzed by the Predictive Unit for Layer Security Evaluation (PULSE), a compact detector trained offline as an ensemble of classifiers and realized on-chip as a small neural engine. For explainability and recovery, BARE-AI introduces an Activation Shift Index (ASI) for layer level fault localization and a z-score based repair that resets anomalous weights toward clean layer statistics. Across CNNs, Vision Transformers, and Large Language Models under random, targeted, adaptive, and magnitude based BFAs, BARE-AI achieves up to 98% detection accuracy on vision models and 74% to 95% on language models, restores near clean accuracy for CNNs and ViTs, and provides partial recovery for LLMs. Synthesized at 28nm, the monitoring infrastructure incurs under 3% energy, under 4% area, and about 10% latency overhead, with a configurable operating point that reduces latency overhead to about 6%. Unlike error correcting codes, whose redundancy grows with the number of tolerated flips, BARE-AI's overhead remains constant regardless of attack strength, making it attractive for resource constrained, safety critical edge applications such as autonomous systems, energy, and healthcare.

title: Automated Lemma Discovery in Agentic Program Verification
abstract: Deductive verification provides strong correctness guarantees for code by extracting verification conditions (VCs) and writing formal proofs for them. The expertise-intensive task of VC proving is the main bottleneck in this process, and has been partly automated owing to recent advances in Large Language Model (LLM) agents. However, existing proof agents are not able to discover helper lemmas -- auxiliary lemmas that aid in proving -- and thus fall short as programs grow in size and complexity. In this paper, we argue that VC proving for program verification is more than a purely mathematical task, and benefits considerably from program comprehension. Our key insight is that human proof engineers often discover and apply helper lemmas based on their understanding of the program semantics, which are not directly reflected in the VCs produced by VC generators. Inspired by this insight, we propose an LLM agent, LemmaNet, that discovers helper lemmas in two ways. Specifically, the agent first synthesizes lemmas offline by directly analyzing the source code and specifications and then relating this semantic understanding to the mechanical, verbose encoding produced by VC generators. As the proof unfolds, LemmaNet then adapts existing helper lemmas online to accommodate evolving proof states, enabling the agent to effectively discharge complex VCs on-the-fly. We implement LemmaNet on top of an existing proof agent AutoRocq for Rocq and the Frama-C ecosystem, and evaluate it on SV-COMP and established real-world subjects, including modules of the Linux kernel, Contiki OS, standard C++ library, and X.509 parser. Our experimental results demonstrate that LemmaNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, highlighting the importance of program comprehension-aided lemma discovery in agentic program verification.

title: Reading the Board, Playing Another One: Turn-Level Evaluation of Open LLM Agents on Textual Sokoban
abstract: Aggregate outcomes hide where an interactive agent fails. We study five open 3-8B LLM agents on textual Sokoban: 180 episodes and 1,561 steps over six conditions, in which no level is solved. Two language-model annotators code each turn against a behavioural taxonomy induced from three blind reading passes. A push-optimal replay through the repaired harness solves every level, and no model solves any of the 60 ladder episodes that need four or more pushes, where random play almost always fails. Two observations are supported, at different strengths. Across the five models, the move a thought describes and the action it emits differ in kind, usually a plain move described and a push emitted: both annotators label this in 111 of 180 episodes (kappa 0.749); in one 32B model, one annotator labels it on none of 172 pushes. The prompt's only worked example has this shape, and a pre-registered arm that made it consistent left its effect unresolved. In the one model that writes its own board table into its thought, an accurate table, probably copied, sits beside prose that reasons from a different board (14 episodes on the reading passes; 6 to 27 of 180 on the annotations). A pre-registered positive control, where 12.76 of 20 solves are chance-expected, finds no separation between solved and unsolved episodes, so the taxonomy is a description, not a validated discriminator.

title: Code and data for "What Does a Machine-Translated Test Set Measure? Provenance Effects in Multilingual Intent Classification"
abstract: Code, run records, per-sentence predictions, machine-translated corpora and human-evaluation sheets for the paper "What Does a Machine-Translated Test Set Measure? Provenance Effects in Multilingual Intent Classification". Contents: Python scripts for all experiments and analyses; per-sentence prediction files and per-run records (results_v2.csv, each row carrying the run’s arguments, device, library versions and timestamps); machine-translated corpora for Korean, Chinese, German, Vietnamese and Japanese produced with facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M, and test-split translations for Korean, Chinese, German and Vietnamese produced with facebook/nllb-200-3.3B; human-evaluation sheets, rubric and the key mapping items to source sentences; the layer-1 and layer-2 registered runs, the case-normalization control and the verdict files. Licences: code MIT; the machine translations in translations/ CC BY-NC 4.0, following the NLLB-200 licence; everything else CC BY 4.0. MASSIVE v1.1 source text is CC BY 4.0. DeepL translations are not redistributed from version 1.1 onward (version 1.0 contained them). Version 1.1 removes the DeepL translations, corrects the mt_source labels of the NLLB translations, and adds the layer-1 and layer-2 registered runs, the case-normalization control and the verdict files (see README_v1.1.md). Translations in translations/ are CC BY-NC 4.0; code is MIT; everything else is CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE.md).

title: Code, predictions and analysis for "What Do Language Models Lose When Vietnamese Loses Its Diacritics? Distribution Shift, Residual Loss and Remedies in Encoders and Few-Shot LLMs"
abstract: Supplementary material of the paper: source code (corruption module, encoder fine-tuning, few-shot LLM evaluation, restoration, analysis), the hash-locked protocol and lock files, per-example predictions and probabilities of 45 encoder runs and 36 LLM runs, analysis tables and figures, and the provenance record (timestamps, code hashes, GPU trace). The input datasets (UIT-VSFC, XNLI, XQuAD, UIT-ViQuAD2.0) are public under their own licences and are not redistributed. Models used: XLM-R base, mBERT, PhoBERT-base-v2, Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and a public restoration model (peterhung/vietnamese-accent-marker-xlm-roberta).

title: Detecção de anomalias em tempo real para identificação de fraudes com streaming data e online learning: uma revisão da literatura
abstract: Resumo A crescente digitalização dos serviços financeiros e das plataformas electrónicas tem intensificado os desafios associados à detecção de fraudes, exigindo sistemas capazes de analisar grandes volumes de dados em tempo real. Os métodos tradicionais, baseados em regras fixas e em modelos estáticos, revelam limitações perante a evolução contínua dos padrões fraudulentos. O presente artigo tem como objectivo analisar, através de uma revisão da literatura, a aplicação da detecção de anomalias em tempo real à identificação de fraudes com recurso a Streaming Data e a algoritmos de Online Learning. O estudo adopta uma abordagem qualitativa, descritiva e exploratória, assente na pesquisa bibliográfica em bases de dados científicas e na análise qualitativa de conteúdo de artigos, livros e estudos especializados nas áreas da Inteligência Artificial, da aprendizagem automática, da mineração de fluxos de dados e da segurança digital. Os resultados evidenciam que a integração entre o processamento contínuo de dados, a detecção de anomalias e a aprendizagem incremental permite desenvolver sistemas mais adaptativos, escaláveis e eficientes na identificação de comportamentos suspeitos. Persistem, contudo, desafios relacionados com o concept drift, o desequilíbrio entre classes, os falsos positivos, a interpretabilidade dos modelos e a validação destas tecnologias em contextos reais, sendo ainda escassos os estudos sobre países em desenvolvimento, incluindo Moçambique. Conclui-se que a combinação entre Streaming Data e Online Learning constitui uma abordagem promissora para reforçar os mecanismos de prevenção de fraudes digitais, recomendando-se o desenvolvimento de estudos empíricos que considerem diferentes contextos tecnológicos e socioeconómicos. Abstract The increasing digitalisation of financial services and electronic platforms has intensified the challenges associated with fraud detection, requiring systems capable of analysing large volumes of data in real time. Traditional methods, based on fixed rules and static models, show limitations in the face of the continuous evolution of fraudulent patterns. This article aims to analyse, through a literature review, the application of real-time anomaly detection to fraud identification using Streaming Data and Online Learning algorithms. The study adopts a qualitative, descriptive and exploratory approach, based on a bibliographic search of scientific databases and on a qualitative content analysis of articles, books and specialised studies in the fields of Artificial Intelligence, machine learning, data stream mining and digital security. The findings show that integrating continuous data processing, anomaly detection and incremental learning enables the development of more adaptive, scalable and efficient systems for identifying suspicious behaviour. However, challenges persist regarding concept drift, class imbalance, false positives, model interpretability and the validation of these technologies in real-world settings, and studies on developing countries, including Mozambique, remain scarce. The study concludes that combining Streaming Data and Online Learning is a promising approach to strengthening digital fraud prevention mechanisms, and recommends empirical studies that consider different technological and socio-economic contexts.

title: Cryptanalysis of multiparty key exchange protocols over a modified supertropical semiring
abstract: We present a cryptanalysis of a multiparty key exchange protocol over a modified supertropical semiring, as proposed in a recent work of R. Ponmaheshkumar, J. Ramalingam, and R. Perumal. Building on the established methods for solving linear systems A⊗x=b over the tropical semiring, as well as on our recent work on solving such systems over layered semirings, such as the symmetrized and supertropical semirings, we develop a method to compute a solution of A⊗x=b over the above mentioned modified supertropical semiring. This method enables the attacker to recover the shared secret key by solving the one-sided linear system derived from the public messages of the protocol. Our findings show that this modified supertropical platform does not provide the intended security and motivate further exploration of secure semiring-based constructions.

title: AI-Mediated Self: How HCI Defines and Relates to the Self
abstract: How might AI alter how we understand and experience the self? This scoping review analyzes 102 papers to examine how the self is defined in the field of human-computer interaction (HCI), how AI-self relationships are conceptualized, and what risks emerge when AI becomes entangled with selfhood. Our synthesis makes three contributions. First, we define AI-mediated self as a conceptual umbrella that connects dispersed work across education, workplace, health, and creative practices. Second, we consolidate six framings of the self with four domains of ethical risk-agency/autonomy, identity/authorship, relational capacity, and meaning-making-into a conceptual map that provides a reusable vocabulary across contexts. Third, we introduce the Inclusion of AI-Self framework, which situates AI-self relationships along a spectrum of proximity. Together, these contributions position selfhood as a central design space in HCI.

title: Efficient Estimation of Logical Sensitivities Through Fault-Counting
abstract: Quantum error-correcting circuits are affected by multiple physical noise mechanisms, whose contributions to logical failure must be understood to evaluate code performance and guide improvements in hardware. The individual error budget contributions for an error type $i$ can be characterized by its logical sensitivity $ν_i = \frac{\partial p_L}{\partial p_i}$, which measures the response of the logical error rate $p_L$ to each physical noise parameter $p_i$. Normally, $ν_i$ is measured using linear fits such as finite differences, where $p_L$ is measured at two or more values of $p_i$ to calculate partial derivatives. In this paper, we develop a differentiable estimator to obtain all components of $\nabla_{\mathbf p}p_L$ simultaneously from a single Monte Carlo data set at one noise configuration, using information about the underlying fault configurations. In surface code simulations with circuit-level noise, the estimator agrees with conventional finite differences while requiring one to two orders of magnitude fewer shots to achieve the same variance. We apply this technique to quantify error budgets, resolve sensitivities at the individual qubit level, and infer effective code distance. Finally, we incorporate the sensitivities into Newton root finding to locate and trace threshold contours in multidimensional noise models. These results provide an efficient method for extracting and applying logical sensitivity information from standard quantum error correction simulations.

title: DeepTopoClustering: Unsupervised Derivation of Surface Process Taxonomy from 4D Point Clouds for Topographic Monitoring
abstract: 4D point clouds acquired by permanent laser scanning (PLS) enable accurate high-frequency monitoring of surface change in dynamic topographic environments. However, existing methods remain limited in organizing detected surface activities into meaningful process types. We propose DeepTopoClustering (DTC), an unsupervised framework for deriving a hierarchical process taxonomy from object-based surface activities, so-called 4D objects-by-change (4D-OBCs). We transform each 4D-OBC into a GeoMorphogram, a distributional sequence representing the temporal evolution of topographic change within a spatially bounded surface activity. A convolutional autoencoder learns latent embeddings from GeoMorphograms, which are jointly optimized using a hierarchical deep clustering objective to organize surface activities into a hierarchy. We evaluate the learned hierarchy using expert annotations on two 4D datasets of sandy beach sites and their combination. DTC with GeoMorphograms achieves the highest agreement with expert judgment at the taxonomy level comprising eight major process types ($F_1=0.78$, match accuracy $=0.92$), outperforming dimensionality reduction and conventional flat clustering. The learned taxonomy separates major erosion- and deposition-dominated activities and distinguishes finer subtypes based on change magnitude, duration, compactness, and temporal evolution. DTC thus provides a scalable and interpretable route from 4D change detection to a data-driven, expert-supported surface process taxonomy, advancing automated knowledge derivation for understanding surface dynamics in topographic monitoring.

title: HSAAI: A Sovereign, Self-Hosted Enterprise AI Platform for Secure RAG, Agentic Workflows, and AI Governance
abstract: HSAAI is a sovereign, self-hosted Enterprise Artificial Intelligence platform designed to provide organizations with secure and governed access to large language models, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI agents, enterprise knowledge, observability, and cloud-native infrastructure while maintaining control over sensitive data and AI operations. This paper presents the architecture, design principles, research questions, and evaluation framework of HSAAI. The platform integrates enterprise RAG, agentic and multi-agent workflows, AI governance, identity and access control, security, LLMOps/MLOps, observability, and containerized deployment within a unified enterprise AI architecture. Particular attention is given to data sovereignty, controlled agent execution, policy enforcement, auditability, self-hosted deployment, Arabic-English enterprise AI, and operational resilience. The paper also defines an empirical evaluation methodology covering retrieval quality, factual faithfulness, agent task success, security-policy enforcement, system performance, reliability, and bilingual enterprise workloads. HSAAI is presented as an engineering and research platform for studying secure, sovereign, governed, and agentic artificial intelligence in enterprise environments. The associated source-code repository and technical artifacts are publicly available through the HSAAI GitHub project.

title: System Hallucination Frequency and Service Failure Recovery in AI-Assisted Heritage Education: Psychological Safety, Collaborative Learning, and Technological Contingencies
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is finding growing use in heritage education, but system hallucinations can impair learning and service recovery in culturally sensitive settings. The associations of System Hallucination Frequency (SHF) with On-Site Service Failure Recovery Effectiveness (SFRE) are examined through Trainee Psychological Safety (TPS) and Trainee Collaborative Learning Behavior (TCLB), with technological contingencies. Data were collected from 427 university students in Saudi Arabia with experience in AI-supported heritage-related learning using a cross-sectional survey. Structural Equation Modeling indicated that higher perceived SHF was negatively associated with SFRE, TPS, and TCLB, whereas TPS and TCLB were positively associated with recovery effectiveness. TPS and TCLB also showed significant individual and serial indirect associations. Moreover, TCLB and perceived retrieval quality (CRA-TKP) buffered the negative SHF-TPS association, and perceived flagging quality (AGFP-CCN) strengthened the positive TCLB-SFRE association. The results identify associations consistent with the proposed AI-mediated service-recovery model and offer practical guidance for designing reliable and culturally sensitive AI-supported heritage education systems.

title: Piecewise weighted linear regression estimation based on Interval Type-2 Gustafson-Kessel fuzzy clustering
abstract: The presence of piecewise linearity in the parameter estimation of regression models necessitates appropriate clustering of the dataset. In this study, a novel multi-strategy algorithm is proposed for piecewise weighted linear regression. First, the optimal number of clusters is determined using a modified Davies–Bouldin Index (DBI), in which the Euclidean distance is replaced by the Mahalanobis distance to better accommodate ellipsoidal data structures. Second, the dataset is partitioned using an extension of the classical Gustafson–Kessel (GK) algorithm based on Interval Type-2 (IT2) fuzzy clustering, where the fuzziness index is defined as an interval rather than a single value. The resulting membership degrees are then employed as weights in the parameter estimation of piecewise weighted linear regression models. The proposed approach is evaluated using three synthetic and three real-world datasets and compared with Fuzzy C Means (FCM), IT2FCM, GK, and K-means methods. Performance is assessed using mean squared error (MSE), convergence iterations, and statistical significance tests. The proposed method achieves average error reductions of 71.58%, 39.76%, 47.99%, and 49.38% compared with FCM, IT2FCM, GK, and K-means, respectively. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests indicate statistically significant improvements, with p-values ranging from 0.0277 to 0.0464. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach provides more accurate parameter estimates for piecewise weighted linear data structures.

title: Strategic Investment Decision Making for Value Creation in Energy Transition: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: The global challenge of climate change has driven significant steps to reduce CO2 emissions, guided by international agreements like the Paris Agreement of 2015. Acting too slowly could result in future losses and reputational damage, while moving too quickly could jeopardize shareholder value due to the marginal profitability or potential losses due to technology immaturity of many renewable projects. To navigate this complex transition, energy companies must adopt Sequential Decision Making (SDM) strategies to maximize value creation from decision flexibility under uncertainties. To support this, we developed a custom simulation environment to model the dynamic energy landscape up to 2050. Building on this, we designed a multi-criteria SDM framework that explores various decision strategies related to different portfolios for allocating funds across three sectors: oil & gas, renewables, and CO2 reduction. It aims to maximize value during the transition while accounting for uncertainties in productions, energy prices, and costs. This framework has three objectives: maximizing profit, minimizing CO2 social costs, and enhancing competitive advantage in the renewable energy sector. This research evaluates the use of Reinforcement Learning (RL) to identify optimal investment policies within the defined SDM framework. The agent's sequential decisions shape a virtual dynamic environment by influencing key variables such as oil and gas production, renewable energy output, CO2 emissions, and revenues. Through repeated interaction, the RL algorithm explores the state space and learns an optimal policy under uncertainty. We benchmark the RL strategy against a set of manually defined baseline policies and find it consistently outperforms them in adaptability and long-term value creation.

title: HarnessIR: Harnessing Multimodal Foundation Models for Universal Real-World Image Restoration
abstract: Real-world low-quality images suffer from complex mixed degradations, including but not limited to noise, blur, atmospheric effects, etc. Recent agentic methods usually model real-world image restoration (Real-IR) as a sequential tool calling problem over task-specific single-degradation restoration models. This paradigm, however, is fundamentally limited because complex real-world degradations cannot be cleanly undone degradation by degradation, and the tool used for task-specific models caps the capability of the agent system. In this work, we present HarnessIR, an agentic framework for Real-IR by harnessing a multimodal foundation model (MFM) as the executor. HarnessIR consists of five stages: perception and diagnosis, on-demand tool invocation, prompt composition, execution, and verification-driven refinement. Unlike prior agentic Real-IR methods that rely on tool chains assembled from task-specific models, HarnessIR feeds the restoration requirements, the perceptual diagnosis, and the evidence into an MFM that performs restoration in a single pass, followed by verification stages to determine whether the result warrants further processing. Under our harness, off-the-shelf MFMs handle restoration tasks remarkably well, achieving state-of-the-art results on the widely used MiO100 synthetic benchmark. More importantly, by exploiting the strong generalization ability of MFMs, HarnessIR delivers compelling restoration quality on challenging real-world scenes where previous agentic IR systems often struggle. Codes is available at https://github.com/PolyU-VCLab/HarnessIR.

title: The Case for Synthesized Data Compression
abstract: Compression is a fundamental tool in data management. Today's compression schemes are generally designed by hand to apply to many different types of data (e.g., run length encoding or arithmetic encoding), leading to a zoo of general-purpose algorithms which work well for many datasets, but may not be optimal for any specific dataset. Inspired by recent advancements in agentic coding, we propose synthesizing custom-tailored data compression algorithms on a per-dataset basis. Unlike prior work using agents to synthesize database components, a data-specific compression algorithm can be fully verified at construction time, alleviating most correctness concerns. Modern file formats, like AnyBlox and F3, allow including the synthesized code alongside the data itself. Experimentally, we show that our synthesis agent can expand the compression-factor/decompression-speed Pareto front, outperforming general-purpose methods by nearly $2\times$ in compression factor.

title: Democratizing MoE inference on commodity GPUs with CoMoE
abstract: Deploying Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models relies heavily on Expert Parallelism, which generates intense inter-GPU communication. Consequently, state-of-the-art inference systems require high-bandwidth, P2P interconnects (e.g., NVLink) in datacenter GPUs to handle massive token routing, making deployment prohibitively expensive. Consumer GPUs offer comparable compute power at significantly lower cost, promising to democratize MoE inference for individuals and enable privacy-preserving local deployments. However, their bandwidth-limited (only weak PCIe bus bandwidth) and host-mediated interconnects (no P2P support) introduce severe communication bottlenecks. We present CoMoE, a communication-efficient MoE inference system that resolves this mismatch through novel host-centric routing. Our key insight is that the unique communication topology provides the opportunity to elevate the host to an active routing hub, which can fundamentally reduce communication volume and eliminate global synchronization-induced stalls. Specifically, for token dispatch, we introduce host-backed token multicast to write shared tokens to the host exactly once, eliminating outbound transmission redundancy. For token combine, we propose a fine-grained, token-level aggregation mechanism using host staging buffers, which replaces rigid global synchronization and mitigates straggler effects. Evaluation on RTX 5090 GPUs shows that CoMoE improves inference throughput by up to 1.46x, approaching the performance of NVLink-capable A800 GPUs at only 23.4% of the hardware cost.

title: RAPO-Sol: Retrieval-Augmented Preference Optimization for Repository-Level Solidity Code Generation
abstract: Smart contracts written in Solidity manage assets, permissions, and irreversible state changes, making code generation both useful and security-critical. Repository-level Solidity generation is challenging because models must synthesize complete contracts or libraries while preserving consistency across state variables, modifiers, events, inheritance, external calls, and access-control logic. We present RAPO-Sol, a two-stage training framework for repository-level Solidity code generation. First, Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning (RAFT) augments each training input with similar Solidity examples, helping the model learn recurring contract-level patterns while remaining retrieval-free at inference time. Second, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) trains the model to prefer reference contracts over close but semantically flawed alternatives. We construct rejected samples using Solidity Semantic-Anchor Perturbation (SAP), which perturbs validation statements, visibility modifiers, data-location keywords, context variables, payment operations, and low-level calls. Experiments on SolidityBench with CodeLlama-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct show that RAFT consistently improves over supervised fine-tuning, while SAP-based DPO provides further gains in BLEU and SolidityScore. The full RAFT+DPO pipeline achieves the best performance across all three models, demonstrating complementary benefits from retrieval during training and Solidity-aware preference optimization without adding retrieval cost at inference.

title: Penerapan Metode Certainty Factor Mendiagnosa Penyakit pada Tanaman Mentimun
abstract: Cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.) is one of the horticultural commodities with economic value and is widely cultivated by farmers, including the BATARA F1 hybrid cucumber variety. However, crop productivity often decreases due to various diseases that show similar symptoms, making it difficult for farmers to accurately identify the type of disease. The problems faced by the Agriculture Office of Binjai City include limited farmers' knowledge and lack of access to agricultural experts in diagnosing cucumber diseases. This study aims to develop an expert system to assist farmers in diagnosing diseases affecting the BATARA F1 hybrid cucumber variety based on the symptoms observed. The method used is the Certainty Factor (CF) method to calculate the level of confidence in the diagnosis based on the symptoms selected by the user. The system provides information including the disease name, Certainty Factor value, confidence percentage, and appropriate treatment recommendations. Based on the test results, Powdery Mildew obtained the highest Certainty Factor value of 0.9923 or 99.23%, indicating a very high level of confidence in the diagnosis. The diagnosis results can also be stored in the diagnostic history and printed as reports. Therefore, the developed expert system can assist farmers in diagnosing cucumber diseases more quickly and provide appropriate treatment information.

title: Explainable Ensemble Learning for Fraud Detection in Decentralized Finance
abstract: Python implementation and Jupyter notebook accompanying the research on explainable ensemble machine learning for fraud detection in decentralized finance (DeFi). Overview: This repository contains the complete experimental pipeline utilizing models including Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Deep Neural Networks (DNN) applied to decentralized finance transaction profiling. It incorporates SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) interpretability analysis, robustness evaluations, and data leakage audits. title: RAG-Based Medical Question Answering Assistant Using Semantic 1 Embedding NLP Technique
abstract: This study presents an implemented Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based Medical QuestionAnswering Assistant that compares a general-purpose semantic embedding model with biomedicaldomain-specific embedding models for medical information retrieval. The implemented system usesthe MedQuAD dataset, a vector database retrieval pipeline, configurable embedding models, and anLLM-based answer generation interface. The prototype supports general-purpose all-MiniLM-L6-v2and domain-specific BioBERT, MedCPT, and BGE-M3 embeddings, with evaluation based onPrecision@k, Recall@k, nDCG, MRR, Accuracy, Faithfulness, BERTScore, and retrieval latency.The system performs proportional stratified evaluation across medical question types and exposesretrieved source passages with source metadata and cosine-similarity scores. Benchmark resultsshown in the implemented system demonstrate that the domain-specific models outperform thegeneral-purpose baseline on the reported retrieval and answer-quality measures, with MedCPTobtaining the strongest overall benchmark values among the compared models. The study reports themeasurement framework, sampling procedure, ethical considerations, and dataset bias.

title: УТИЦАЈ ПРИМЕНЕ ИНФОРМАЦИОНИХ СИСТЕМА НА ПЕРСОНАЛИЗОВАНО ОБРАЗОВАЊЕ: ЕМПИРИЈСКА АНАЛИЗА
abstract: Развој и примена информационих система (ИС) у образовању омогућава персонализован приступ учењу прилагођен индивидуалним потребама, способностима и интересовањима студената. Савремене дигиталне технологије омогућавају прикупљање и анализу података о напретку корисника, што помаже бољем разумевању стилова учења и динамике усвајања наставних садржаја. На основу прикупљених података, систем може препоручити одговарајуће наставне материјале, задатке и активности, чиме се омогућава ефикасније и флексибилније учење. Посебан значај има примена вештачке интелигенције (ВИ), машинско учење и аналитика учења, које омогућавају адаптивно учење и континуирано праћење напретка. Истраживање спроведено на узорку од 160 студената Факултета техничких наука у Чачку Универзитета у Крагујевцу показало је да ИС значајно побољшава мотивацију, разумевање наставних садржаја и ефикасност учења, док наставницима пружа бољи увид у напредак студената и омогућава квалитетније планирање наставе. Резултати t-тест анализе показују да је средња вредност статистички значајно различита од референтне вредности (t(160) = 32.5; p < 0.05), што потврђује значај утицаја примене ИС на квалитет и персонализацију образовног процеса. Континуирана примена ИС у персонализацији образовања представља значајан корак ка модернизацији образовног система и развоју дигиталног учења.

title: Unified Field Theory of Human Behavior: Operator–Functor–Response Framework Across Disciplines
abstract: This project introduces a transdisciplinary structural framework—Unified Field Theory of Human Behavior—that explains human, social, and artificial behavior through a single, coherent mathematical and conceptual architecture. The theory is built on three core principles: every system possesses an invariant internal structure; no universal, context‑independent behavioral rules exist; and all observable behavior emerges from context‑driven response dynamics. The framework models environments, interpretations, and behaviors as structured categories, and describes responses as mappings between them. This approach unifies insights from mathematics, physics, semiotics, psychology, cognitive science, social science, artificial intelligence, and narrative theory. It provides a seven‑level hierarchy of applications, ranging from character and narrative design to large‑scale social transitions and AI cognition. The project also develops several advanced extensions: dynamic evolution of the invariant core, non‑commutative behavioral structures, multi‑agent simulation architectures, operator‑splitting numerical schemes, and empirical methods for identifying effective behavioral operators. These extensions allow the theory to function not only as a conceptual meta‑framework but also as a foundation for computational modeling and interdisciplinary research.

title: CPU-Auth: Device Fingerprinting for Authentication via DVFS Side-Channel
abstract: Lack of effective authentication has resulted in numerous security and privacy breaches, including unauthorized access to protected information, identity theft, and fraud. One approach to mitigating such attacks is Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), in which users must provide multiple pieces of information for authentication. Some secondary authentication factors include SMS text verification codes, biometrics, and tokens. Each contains at least one notable flaw: SMS is notoriously insecure; biometrics rely upon access to sensitive personal data; and tokens require dependence on third-party providers (e.g. OAuth providers). This work explores CPU-Auth, a novel authentication mechanism based on unique variations in the physical characteristics of the CPU of a computing device. By measuring the behavior of the Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) governor remotely from within a browser, unique properties of the CPU can be leveraged to establish a hardware-based device fingerprint for use in CPU-Auth. The performance of CPU-Auth is evaluated on over 50,000 data traces using distance-based and deep learning methods. CPU-Auth is part of a larger research project, and the results provided in this report reflect only the contributions made to the project by members of this group.

title: When Algorithmic Exploration Becomes Cheap: A Case Study of Agentic Research in EDA
abstract: As EDA researchers, we conducted eight deliberate trials of agentic algorithm exploration, selecting several topics outside our areas of depth. One faculty member and seven students participated, including students without publication experience. With limited intervention in the algorithms, agents developed mathematical constructions, analyzed existing tools, and implemented improvements; some efforts fell short of their practical goals. We also used AI to collect, classify, and analyze 8,420 papers from four EDA conferences and two journals over 2022-2026. Among 2,380 primary-core papers, we classified 97.7% from titles and abstracts as computationally closed, including work on new formulations. Together, these observations suggest that much of EDA offers an executable environment for increasingly accessible algorithm research. We see an opportunity for tool developers to investigate ideas they previously lacked time to pursue. We also ask how EDA should validate and reward research when results become easier to produce than to examine, and what papers and venue labels will continue to tell us about a contribution.

title: Spatial Latent Reasoning for Embodied Reference Understanding
abstract: Pointing-gesture visual grounding requires connecting hand geometry with the visual identity and extent of a referred object. A central challenge for continuous latent reasoning is how to organize these complementary cues into useful intermediate supervision. We propose Spatial Latent Reasoning (SLR), a framework that structures this supervision around an ordered sequence of geometric and visual states. A spatial ray state is supervised by fingertip position and pointing direction, followed by four states aligned with target-region features. To construct the visual targets, we introduce parity pooling, which applies polyphase grouping to average region tokens on four interleaved spatial supports. All states are generated recurrently during training and inference; auxiliary annotations are required only during training. On EgoPoint-Ground, the framework improves mIoU over same-backbone supervised fine-tuning by 2.8, 17.5, and 21.1 percentage points on Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and Qwen3-VL-8B, respectively, with improvements on both hard subsets. On YouRefIt, it achieves 77.6% precision at IoU 0.5, a numerical margin of 5.2 percentage points over the reported state of the art under differing evaluation protocols. Ablations support joint geometric and visual supervision on the standard and similar-object sets, and favor parity over three alternative pooling operators on the standard set. These results support task-structured supervision for continuous pointing grounding. We will release the code and supporting materials.

title: AN AUTOENCODER-BASED UNSUPERVISED FRAUD DETECTION FRAMEWORK FOR NIGERIAN BANKING TRANSACTIONS
abstract: The Nigerian banking sector faces a critical and escalating challenge with financial fraud that threatens the sustainability and trustworthiness of electronic banking services. Despite significant investments in security infrastructure and fraud prevention systems, Nigerian banks continue to experience substantial financial losses due to fraudulent activities. Financial fraud in banking systems is sparse, adaptive, and costly to monitor with fixed rule sets. To this effect, this paper presents an unsupervised autoencoder framework that learns the patterns of legitimate transactions and identifies suspicious activity using the reconstruction error of a symmetric autoencoder. The empirical evaluation uses the PaySim mobile money dataset, which contains 6,362,620 transactions and a fraud rate of 0.13 percent. After preprocessing through data cleaning, normalisation, feature encoding, and dimensionality reduction, eight numerical features remain for model training. The symmetric autoencoder converges after 11 epochs, and the anomaly threshold is set at the 95th percentile of the training reconstruction-error distribution, 0.001114. On the held-out test set, the model attains precision of 1.00%, recall of 38.96%, F1-score of 1.95%, specificity of 95.01%, accuracy of 94.94%, and AUC-ROC of 0.7338. The results indicate a useful screening mechanism for settings where labels are scarce, noisy, or unavailable. The framework is most significant as a first-stage detector that supports analyst review rather than as a final autonomous decision engine
